articleTitle: Calculation of the Proper Auxiliary Circuit Phase Number for Multiphase Stacked Interleaved Buck Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: A multiphase stacked interleaved buck converter (SIBC) ensures the cancellation of current ripple across all duty cycles. However, to achieve ripple cancellation, the auxiliary circuit in the multiphase SIBC must operate at a higher switching frequency than the main circuit. In this paper, we propose a calculation method to determine the proper number of auxiliary circuit phases in multiphase SIBCs, aiming to reduce the switching frequency of the auxiliary circuit by increasing its phase configuration. The effects of the auxiliary circuit phase number on output current ripple, inductor volume index, and DC-blocking capacitor requirements of the multiphase SIBC are also analyzed. The proposed phase number for the auxiliary circuit is validated through simulation, with a focus on output current ripple cancellation.

articleTitle: Influence of Background Color on 6D Pose Tracking Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Fast 6D pose tracking is a critical component in numerous applications ranging from robotics to augmented reality. A notable method for addressing this challenge involves simulating the last known pose and comparing it with the current one, a process central to the SE(3)-TrackNet approach, which is known for its reliability. Traditionally, this method employs a uniform black background for the simulated input. This study challenges the standard practice by demonstrating that the choice of background color can significantly influences the accuracy of 6D pose estimation. Through a series of experiments, we provide results showing that background color is a critical factor for the effectiveness of the SE(3) TrackNet approach.

articleTitle: Predicting Photovoltaic Power Generation in Pakistan Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is central to energy management and integrating renewable energy into the electricity grid network. This study considered environmental data, namely, Global Horizontal Irradiance (GHI), temperature, relative humidity, wind speed, and rainfall data obtained from NASA's Prediction of Worldwide Energy Resources (POWER) project to estimate the PV power generation in Pakistan. The PV generation dataset of Pakistan is trained using three machine learning algorithms: XGBoost, LightGBM, and Random Forest. The performance of the proposed machine learning algorithm is assessed by Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and R-squared (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). The evaluations suggest that LightGBM has the smallest RMSE (0.7116), the lowest MAE (0.3922), and the highest R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (0.99997), which proves its enhanced accuracy and robustness. The study reveals that environmental factors are crucial in solar PV power forecasting and identified GHI and temperature as the most important predictors of PV power output.

articleTitle: ARLClustering: R Package for Community Detection-Based Association Rules Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Community detection in social networks is a cornerstone of social network analysis, yet traditional methods often overlook the intricate interaction patterns between nodes, focusing instead on topological measures such as modularity or centrality. To address these limitations, this paper presents ARLClustering, an R package that employs association rule mining (ARM) through the Apriori algorithm to identify communities based on frequent interaction patterns. By leveraging ARM, ARLClustering uncovers nuanced relational structures, enabling the detection of meaningful and interpretable communities in complex networks. The used methodology involves transforming network data into a transactional format suitable for ARM, identifying frequent itemsets, and extracting communities from association rules. This approach is validated across diverse datasets (e.g. Karate Club, Dolphins, and Facebook networks and so on). A Comparative analysis highlights ARLClustering's important performance in detecting granular clusters and managing high volumes of network data while maintaining computational efficiency. Key contributions include its open-source accessibility, user-friendly design, and robust handling of parameter sensitivity for support and confidence thresholds. Beyond theoretical advancements, ARLClustering provides a practical R package for researchers, with comprehensive documentation and visualization features enabling comparative insights with traditional methods. Future work will enhance its visualization techniques, refine cluster evaluation metrics, and expand real-world applications to broaden its impact. Published on CRAN and available on GitHub, ARLClustering stands as a significant step forward in association rule-based community detection, bridging the gap between traditional methods and the demand for deeper relational insights in social network analysis.

articleTitle: Light Quantization with Classical Fields in Strong Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: In this paper is demonstrated that quantum ef-fects can be derived in a straightforward manner from the classical radiation intensity equation. To accomplish this, it is employed the equation done by Hartemann and Kerman inside the framework of Nonlinear Compton backscattering. Thus, through mathematical procedures involving the usage of integer-order Bessel functions, it is derived expressions that are in fully agreement to the quantum mechanics formulation of coherence as the one given by Glauber by which a Gaussian profile is representing the coherent states of light. The resulting classical field of emission is interpreted from the spectrum consisting of classical radiated energy against Doppler frequency. It has yielded peaks that are been interpreted ad emitted photons.

articleTitle: Development of IoT Based Smart System and Data Acquisition for Patient Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: In today's busy lifestyle of people it is difficult to maintain health and keep track of patient's health related issues. This problem gets further difficult due to low doctors to patients' ratio in the under-developed countries. However, the advancement in the field of ICT has brought smartness to the medical field. The Internet of Things is rapidly transforming medical technology and famously known as Internet of Medical Things (IoMT). Therefore, in this research work an IoT based smart and cost-effective patient monitoring system has been developed. The vital signs of the patient such as temperature, heart rate, and oxygen level have been measured through sensors and provided at the ESP-32, an internet enabled microcontroller. The acquired data will be transmitted through internet to the gateway and a dashboard is designed using the MQTT protocol for its visualization purpose.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Survival Prediction in Pediatric Kidney Transplantation: A Comprehensive Model for Improved Post-Transplant Outcomes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Kidney transplantation is the optimal treatment for pediatric patients with end-stage renal disease. Accurate survival prediction post-transplantation is essential for improving patient outcomes and tailoring medical decisions. This paper presents a survival prediction model using the Deeplearning4J Multi-Layer Perceptron classifier, specifically designed for pediatric kidney transplant recipients with living donors. We utilized a real-world dataset including pediatric patient records collected from United Network for Organ Sharing consisting of clinical, demographic, and transplant-specific factors to train and evaluate the model. Top ranked attributes were selected through dimensionality reduction technique with ten-fold cross validation. Experimental results with performance evaluation show that the proposed classifier outperforms traditional machine learning models, with significant improvements in predictive accuracy of 92.8%, achieving an Area Under the Curve of 0.913. To prove the accuracy of model, the results were compared with existing approaches and machine learning techniques.

articleTitle: BRAILLAI: A Two Way Web-Based Braille Translation Using Convolutional Neural Network with Gamified E-Learning System Applied for Moderately Visually Impaired and Sighted Individuals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This research introduces a web-based platform designed that utilizes convolutional neural networks along with a gamified e-learning approach. Aimed at both moderately visually impaired and sighted users, The platform leverages sophisticated Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models to effectively translate text into Braille and vice versa, facilitating smooth communication among users with varying visual abilities. This research addresses BRAILLAI's effectiveness in enhancing Braille understanding and its capacity to connect visually impaired and sighted communities, thereby contributing to a more inclusive society. The project underwent testing in accordance with ISO 25010. The results by phase of the study test results demonstrated high levels of functional suitability, performance efficiency, reliability, and usability, as outlined by the ISO model. Moderately Visually Impaired and Sighted Individuals rated the functional suitability, performance efficiency, reliability and usability with means ranging from 4.9 to 4.49, indicating a “Very Good” level of quality, affirming the application's adherence to ISO standards and requirements. These findings underscore the positive performance of the website across all evaluated criteria, showcasing its effectiveness in meeting the needs of both Moderately Visually Impaired and the Sighted individuals. Furthermore, the findings indicate that the integration of computer vision technology with educational content delivery can provide effective learning experiences for diverse learners in language learning.

articleTitle: Global Inflation Data Modeled by Commutative and Non-Commutative Algebra
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: According the global data, global inflation data has exhibited ups and downs along a period of 20 years. One can wonder if the whole dataset can be merely represented by mathematical operations. In this paper, such operations are based in operators that can be satisfying well-defined algebra dictated by commutative as well as non-commutative operations. When operators acts onto continue functions, various relationships can be derived, From these mathematical operations, interpretation of global inflation can be extracted. It is done within the statistical errors and bias associated to operations of commutation that can be also seen as coarse algebra without any correlation to pandemics. Proposed theory and real data are directly confronted and discussed.

articleTitle: Advancing Wearables: Dual-Band Antenna Design with High Permittivity Miniaturization using Natural Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on the design of dual-band antennas using high-permittivity substrates derived from natural materials, specifically Typha angustifolia (Cellulose). The process of this natural substrate is compared with conventional FR4 and an unconventional textile substrate, jeans material. The synthesis is carried out through detailed simulations, focusing on return loss, gain, and radiation pattern. This research highlights the benefits of using natural substrates in terms of flexibility, environmental friendliness, and antenna miniaturization

articleTitle: Optimization of Voltage Windows for Lithium- Ion Cells and Vanadium Redox Flow Battery: An Experimental Investigation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The battery parameters and their interdependencies playa vital role in the operation and health of the battery system. However, the existing co-relation of these parameters is not properly defined, often neither quantitatively nor qualitatively. Voltage window, an important parameter to ascertain battery operations, refers to the voltage range in which the battery can safely operate while maintaining its performance. A large voltage window can lead to challenges in voltage regulation - design constraints and power management complexity, efficiency variability, thermal management challenges, component stress, battery degradation, BMS complexity, user experience, and many others. Economic design of battery system involves trade-offs between voltage range, capacity (range of SoC operation), and component requirement. In the current research, a quantitative analysis of voltage variation with SoC for three different Li-ion chemistries and vanadium redox flow batteries is analyzed through experimentation. The variations are compared, and a considerable reduction in voltage regulation is observed when the operating SoC range is optimized. It is found that operating the battery in the range of 5%-95% SoC can result in a reduction of the operating voltage range by 36–83 %, depending on the battery type. Operating the battery in the curtailed SoC range also enhances its efficiency.

articleTitle: Manipulation of Polaritonic Interferometer in Two-Dimensional Hybrid Organic-Inorganic Perovskite Microcavity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This research explores the manipulation of polaritonic interferometers within two-dimensional hybrid organic-inorganic perovskite microcavities. Utilizing numerical simulations based on the extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation, the study investigates the behavior of polaritons in response to variations in potential strength in the upper arm of the interferometer. These variations in potential strength, attributed to differences in the cavity thickness, show significant correlations with polariton dynamics. Notably, increasing the potential strength in the upper arm leads to considerable modifications in both the spatial distribution and output intensity of polaritons. Specifically, higher potential strengths are associated with delayed propagation and decreased output intensities. To ensure accurate boundary treatments, the study implements perfectly matched layer conditions and employs the fourth-order Runge-Kutta method for precise numerical solutions. These findings enhance the understanding of polariton control in microcavities and demonstrate the potential for manipulation in polaritonic interferometers, contributing to the advancement of next-generation optoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: Development of Indigenous Protocol Testing Platform for Smart and Static Energy Meters Adhering Indian Standards
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: In the present scenario, the deployment of AMI and the smart grid requires smart energy meters with minimum quality and compliance. Since the meters are interoperable and adhere to the open protocol standards, the vital part of the qualification process is the protocol testing to guarantee the meters' compliance. Even though many proprietary and foreign tools are available for conformance and parameter testing, they have limitations such as non-interoperability and lack of economic viability. The suggested smart meter testing tool is an indigenously developed, interoperable, and economically feasible tool for testing the conformance, functionality, communicability, and security of smart energy meters. The features of the indigenously developed smart meter testing tool are described in this paper.

articleTitle: India's V2X Future: C-V2X vs. DSRC - A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The next generation of automotive vehicles will unlikely succeed without connectivity. Automakers and infrastructure developers worldwide currently use two distinct V2X wireless communication technologies i.e. Dedicated Short-Range Communications (DSRC) and Cellular Vehicle-to-Everything (C-V2X). Vehicles use these low-latency communication technologies to communicate with each other (V2V), with road users (V2P), and with infrastructure or mobile networks (V2I). These technologies have enhanced the safety, reliability, and efficiency of the transportation system, while also improving mobility. This paper discusses the performance and evaluation of these two technologies for vehicular communication. Various communication parameters such as range, PER, IPG, and latency were evaluated under different conditions both in the lab and field for both technologies. This study contributes to a better comprehension of these technologies and provides valuable insights for India's future implementations of connected vehicle technology.

articleTitle: Interleaved Reconfigurable-Bridge LLC Resonant Converter with Ultrawide Voltage Range
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper proposes an interleaved reconfigurable-bridge LLC resonant converter for wide output voltage range applications. The converter is reconfigurable through different switching patterns depending on the output voltage conditions, achieving four operation modes: bridge change, effective turns ratio adjustment, and phase shift of the primary-and secondary-side switches. Therefore, the output voltage gain is significantly expanded while achieving a narrow switching frequency range. This allows for selection of an appropriate magnetizing inductance, and significantly reduces circulating current and conduction losses. It also reduces voltage and current stress by achieving zero-voltage switching of the MOSFETs at full load. To verify the performance of the proposed converter, a 3.3 kW rated converter with 400 V input and 150 V-1000 V output is designed.

articleTitle: Graph Neural Network Based on Spectral Parameter Estimation for Mobile Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: For online learning, Graph Neural Networks(GNNs) often require real graph data for parameter fine-tuning, but obtaining the graph data is challenging. Currently, GNNs are trained based on existing graph data. When learning in dynamic networks, spatial-domain GNNs use the adjacency matrix of entire graphs as its input, which are extremely resource-intensive in terms of computation and storage while dealing with large-scale graph data. Moreover, spectral-domain GNNs suffer from high spectral decomposition complexity. To enhance the generalization of GNN models and achieve lightweight GNN models, this paper proposes a lightweight GNN model based on spectral domain, SDGAT(Spectral-Domain Graph Attention Network). By combining spectral domain graph convolution and attention mechanism, SDGAT can effectively capture the global structure and local features of a graph, which helps to suppress noise in the graph and improve the robustness of the model. Furthermore, a distributed estimation algorithm for dynamic network spectral parameters is proposed, which significantly reduces the computational overhead when processing large-scale graph data. Finally, authors validate the effectiveness and accuracy of SDGAT through classification and regression tasks, and explore the feasibility of extending this model to other GNNs.

articleTitle: Parasitic Patch Antenna with Beam Switching for 5G Millimeter-Wave Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper presents a novel millimeter-wave (mmWave) antenna design for 5G applications, featuring a parasitic elliptical patch antenna with beam-switching capabilities and coaxial feeding. The antenna was initially designed as a single-element patch antenna for the 28 GHz mmWave band, demonstrating favorable impedance matching and broadside radiation patterns. Circular parasitic patches with and without vias were strategically placed around the main radiator to enhance the radiation pattern and gain. The single-element design achieved an impedance bandwidth of 2.7 GHz (26.8-29.5 GHz) and a gain of 7.5 dBi at 28 GHz. The optimized parasitic structure, consisting of carefully positioned open and short circular patches, significantly improved the antenna's performance. The parasitic design exhibited an enhanced return loss of -30.5 dB, indicating excellent impedance matching, and a gain of approximately 8 dBi. The proposed antenna exhibits enhanced performance characteristics in terms of gain, return loss, and beam steering capabilities, and it is suitable for next-generation wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Distributed Consensus Computing Problem Over Heterogeneous Opportunistic Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper investigates the distributed consensus computing problem over heterogeneous opportunistic networks with heterogeneity in communication, caching and computing power. In existing work on distributed consensus, the features of heterogeneous opportunistic networks have not been fully considered. This paper combines communication theory and control theory. It first introduces the quantified cache mechanism, proves the stability of the cache queue using Lyapunov drift, and designs a system protocol suitable for heterogeneous opportunistic networks. Secondly, it proves the systemic consensus and analyzes the impacts of delay, packet loss, and topological switching period on convergence. Finally, to accelerate the protocol convergence, the authors use ADMM and gradient descent methods to optimize the weight matrix, cache blocks and control sequences.

articleTitle: Developing Accurate Sri Lankan Sign Language to Tamil Vocal And American Sign Language Translation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This research presents a web-based real-time Sri Lankan Sign Language (SLSL) translation system aimed at bridging communication gaps for individuals with speech and hearing disabilities. Leveraging advanced machine learning, the system translates SLSL gestures into Tamil vocal language and American Sign Language (ASL), supported by video-to-text conversion with Yolo-NAS, voice model and clips of animated 3D characters. Key objectives included accurate vocabulary mapping for selected vocabularies, real-time translation with minimal latency, an audio player to display Tamil voice and animated 3D characters to convey nuanced ASL gestures. The system is integrated as one website, but each translation part has separate pages where users can navigate and fulfill their needs. User feedback highlighted the simple and direct user interface design and fluidity of interactions, particularly the animated 3D characters in SLSL to ASL translation. Challenges included optimizing gesture rendering and expanding vocabulary coverage, which will be addressed in future work. This research underscores the potential of AI-driven solutions for enhancing accessibility and inclusivity in communication with cross-lingual and cross-model communication features.

articleTitle: Dynamic Demand Forecasting with AI: Maximizing Supply Chain Value
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a dynamic demand forecasting platform designed to predict demand accurately and quantify its added value in supply chain management using advanced machine learning and operations management algorithms. The platform collects and processes real-time data from multiple sources, including point-of-sale systems, e-commerce transactions, competitor pricing, weather conditions, and consumer sentiment data. By integrating environmental and product-specific factors, the platform optimizes inventory levels, delivery routing, and operational efficiency. It achieves superior predictive accuracy by leveraging models such as XGBoost and Support Vector Regression (SVR), which consistently outperform traditional methods. The solution is designed to be scalable, cost-effective, and user-friendly, making it particularly accessible to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) that often struggle to implement advanced forecasting systems due to technological and financial constraints. The system's implementation significantly enhances decision-making processes, resulting in reduced operational costs and improved customer satisfaction.

articleTitle: Blockchain Consensus Algorithm Using Cellular Networks Location Services
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper proposes an innovative block validation algorithm for blockchain solutions using cellular network location services. The concept involves using the range of telecommunications signal antennas combined with end-user device position, provided by location services, to generate and solve the consensus task, which involves a race-like challenge with the winner being rewarded, as an additional incentive.

articleTitle: Optimizing DC-DC Buck-Boost Converters with a PID Controller: Harnessing the Power of Silicon Carbide Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The DC-DC buck-boost SiC base that was shown in this research uses a PID controller converter and primarily displays a slightly lower output voltage than the input voltage. With the exception of the SiC Schottky diode, PID controller, paired inductors, and switching capacitor, it is composed of the same components as a traditional DC-DC buck boost converter. The efficiency of the suggested DC-DC buck boost SiC base employing PID controller converter and traditional DC-DC buck boost converter have been compared and contrasted utilizing a PSIM simulation. The outcome demonstrates that, in terms of both switching frequency and load change, the suggested DC-DC buck boost SiC base employing PID controller converter has a greater efficiency than the traditional DC-DC buck boost converter. In order to use inverter power supplies and consume less power and operate more efficiently, modern electronic devices require clean energy.

articleTitle: Private 5G MIMO for Cable TV IP Broadcasting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Private 5G utilization by cable TV is expected to be an alternative to wired services, especially for multi-dwelling units and rural communal TV receiving areas. On the other hand, the 100 MHz of the sub-6 frequency band for private 5G is not sufficient for cable TV services consisting of multi-channel broadcasting and Internet, and some measures to improve frequency utilization efficiency are needed. In this paper, we propose a hybrid MIMO technology for private 5G that applies diversity MIMO for reliable broadcasting and multi-stream MIMO for efficient data communication at the same time.

articleTitle: Optimising Sensor Locations and Enhancing Preventive Maintenance in Steel Trusses Using Finite Element Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Truss systems are widely used in nuclear facilities due to their structural efficiency and load-bearing capabilities; they are critical for maintaining operational safety. However, they require effective monitoring to detect early signs of fatigue, stress, and potential failure. This paper explores the application of finite element analysis (FEA) in optimising sensor placement and enhancing predictive maintenance strategies for truss systems in the nuclear industry. This research found that FEA successfully identifies the areas of maximum stress within a truss and can predict a time frame of defects developing into potential failure. The paper goes on to provide insights for the strategic placement of sensors, ensuring that key locations prone to wear or damage are effectively monitored. The outcomes aim to improve predictive maintenance in engineering and enhance safety by preventing catastrophic failure in members.

articleTitle: Enhancing Smart Home Automation: Secure AC Control and Environmental Monitoring with MQTT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: In line with the advancements in Internet of Things (loT) technology and its wide range of applications, this paper presents a secure AC control switch bot with an environmental monitoring system, using the loT concepts and the MQTT communication protocol. The system integrates a servo motor, a DHTII sensor, and an LED to monitor and control environmental parameters. The Raspberry Pi (RPi) collects temperature and humidity data and publishes it via MQTT to the NodeMCU (ESP8266) micro-controller, which controls the servo motor to press the AC's on/off button based on specified temperature thresholds in a conditional statement. The main objective is to use two MQTT topics to manage the servo motor and LED, based on data received by the RPi and the secure web interface. The RPi functions as a publisher and broker, ensuring secure communication through TLS/SSL encryption and user authentication to overcome ongoing data cyber threats. This research demonstrates a practical and secure approach to 10T-based environmental control, highlighting its potential in smart home automation.

articleTitle: Development of Sensor-Embedded Real-time Posture Monitoring Shirt: Enhancing the Awarness for Healthy Posture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Spinal disorders caused by bad posture have become a major concern in recent years. The slanting for a long duration during work and loading large weight on the body plays a substantial role in the deterioration of posture. To prevent and treat spinal disorders, a real-time posture monitoring device is needed which can monitor posture during daily activities. For this purpose, a real-time wearable smart posture monitoring shirt has been developed. The shirt is designed by using a multiplexer, Bluetooth module, lithium battery, and microcontroller along with Arduino Nano which were interfaced with three MPU 6050 sensors placed on Cervical-1, Thoracic-5, and Lumber-5 to monitor and visualize the posture in real-time. The microcontroller Arduino Nano was programmed by Arduino IDE Software in which complementary filter was implemented. The data processed by the microcontroller was visualized on the mobile app through a Bluetooth module. The results show that the smart shirt can be used for objective measurement of posture in rehabilitation, sports, and medicine. The smart posture monitoring shirt is washable, lightweight, economical, user friendly and provides quantitative information during sitting, standing, and walking. The analysis of the data can be used to maintain a normal posture that can prevent and treat spinal disorders.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis Of The Performance Of Vector And Neural Controls For Industrial Applications: Case Of A Flour Mill
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This article compares the performance of classical vector control and neural control for asynchronous motors, which are essential in industry. Improving the control of these motors is crucial for optimizing their performance and efficiency. While various control strategies have been explored, gaps remain in terms of robustness, stability, and speed, especially when comparing classical and intelligent methods. The objective of the study is to analyze and compare these two approaches to determine which one offers the best performance in an industrial context. Simulations conducted in Matlab/Simulink show that neural control outperforms vector control in terms of regulation, stability, and responsiveness, paving the way for future research on optimizing intelligent control systems.

articleTitle: Tourism Enhancement Through Hybrid Mobile Application with Web Scraping and Recommendation System Using KNN and MF
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Mobile applications have become an essential part of daily life. The tourists develop their tourist attractions and other facilities, which were being struggled after making plans within constraints. However, it is still incomplete and calls for some fine-tuning mechanisms with a view to creating the ideal tourist itinerary. This research has proposed a hybrid mobile app that integrates web scraping with machine learning technology to enhance the trip experience of visitors. The software does web scraping to scrape data in real time from several sites for bookings of hotels, flights, cabs, and food services with one interface. In solving the challenge of personalized tour planning, this app makes use of powerful machine learning techniques: K-Nearest Neighbors and matrix factorization-based recommendation algorithms. These algorithms consider user preferences for budget, length of travel, ratings, and other constraints while making personalized recommendations for tourism sites and activities. Software is constantly reacting to user feedback and behavior to enhance the relevance of recommendations over time. Unique in its method, it enables trip planning not only by unifying services but also makes sure travelers make informed and cost-effective decisions. It represents a huge step forward in intelligent, user-centric travel solutions by embedding the powers of web scraping for extensive data gathering and machine learning for personalization.

articleTitle: Optimizing Video Resolution for Machine Learning-Based Traffic Monitoring Systems: A Performance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This study explores the impact of video resolution on the performance of machine learning-based traffic monitoring systems. Using a combination of empirical analysis and theoretical modeling, we assess how different resolutions affect detection accuracy, resource consumption, and computational efficiency. While other factors such as noise level, or compression artifacts also influence performance, resolution was chosen as a primary variable due to its critical role in balancing detail capture and computational cost. Higher resolutions can enhance object detection accuracy but also significantly increase data processing demands, making resolution a key trade-off in designing efficient surveillance systems. Findings of this study show significant insights into these trade-offs, guiding transportation authorities and system developers in making informed decisions to design scalable traffic monitoring solutions that meet the demands of modern urban environments.

articleTitle: Predicting Air Quality in Pakistan with a Focus on Smog Formation: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Smog is a pressing environmental and public health challenge in Pakistan, particularly in the Punjab province, where rapid urbanization, industrial emissions, and vehicular pollution contribute to a significant rise i n p articulate matter concentrations. The persistent increase in PM2.5 and PM10 levels has exacerbated air quality degradation, leading to frequent smog episodes that disrupt daily life, harm respiratory health, and strain the economy. Accurate forecasting of particulate matter is crucial for the healthcare sector of any country. To achieve, this study aims to develop a predictive model for air quality with a focus on smog formation, leveraging Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) to analyze and forecast PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations. Using historical air quality and meteorological data from key urban centers in Pakistan, the ANN model was trained and validated to capture complex patterns influencing smog events. Preliminary results demonstrate the model's high accuracy in predicting air quality indices and identifying critical thresholds for smog occurrence.

articleTitle: Predictive Modelling of Diabetes Using Ensemble Classifiers: Findings from a Large and Integrated Data Set
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: In this research paper, we examine which of a number of machine learning classifiers are able to predict diabetes in a dataset of 100,000 cases where features include gender, age, state, binary health indicators, smoking, body mass index (BMI), and glucose level, one of which was known to be diabetic. Extensive exploratory data analysis was undertaken to explore the distribution and the relationships between features of the data set and these predictions. Support Vector Machine (SVM), Voting Classifier (VC), and Stacking Classifier (SC). The output of these models was then evaluated with the help of measures using metrics like accuracy, AUC-ROC, and Precision-Recall curves. (Hasan, 2020). The highest accuracy of 98.75% was achieved by the voting classifier (VC), Random Forest (RF) was second with 97.18%, and XGBoost was 3rd with 97.15%. The results of this research can be applied in diabetes prediction, with an important conclusion on how ensemble methods could improve the accuracy indicators for healthcare applications.

articleTitle: Eulerian-DL Forecasting of Wind Turbulence for Wind Turbines: Enabling Smart Sustainable Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Currently, wind power is the fastest-growing sus-tainable energy resource, and accurately predicting wind velocity for individual turbines is essential. Wind behavior is turbulent, with variable patterns, characteristics, and unpredictable extreme events. Moreover, the wind reaching each turbine is impacted by wake loss effects from surrounding turbines, which underscores the need for a precise local prediction model for each turbine to enhance accuracy in smart wind power production. This study proposes a novel approach using local measurements at fixed points, adopting the Eulerian perspective in fluid dynamics to forecast wind turbulence for the coming hour using a deep learning model. A long short-term memory (LSTM) forecasting model is tuned and applied. Laboratory data from wind tunnel tests are utilized to account for velocity fluctuations and wake loss effects, aiming to establish similarity to an affected single wind turbine. Model training and inference run on the high-performance computing (HPC) DEEP-DAM systems at the Julich Supercomputing Centre. Three train-test datasets are employed to evaluate the model. The measured metrics indicate that the mean absolute error is 0.048, the root mean square error is approximately 0.065, and the Pinball loss for the 90th percentile is 0.0042. The model demonstrates a robust predictive capability, supporting the development of advanced instruments for individ-ual turbines and facilitating smart, clean, and sustainable energy production.

articleTitle: Enhanced Load Frequency Control Using PSO-Tuned PID Controller in Two-Area Interconnected Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: LFC is significant in controlling stability within interconnected power systems, and many techniques are available in the literature for this process. This paper proposes an application of PSO for tuning PID controllers to improve LFC in two areas of thermal power systems. Both areas are interfaced with PSO-tuned PID controllers, and the tuning parameters are optimized using PSO to enhance response characteristics. The newly derived method is compared to the traditional Ziegler-Nichols tuning method for validation. The simulation results present that the proposed method of tuning the PID controllers with the help of the PSO algorithm provides better control with minimized settling time and number of oscillations, thereby validating the method. All the simulations are carried out in MATLAB/SIMULINK and offer a general system to assess the effectiveness of the controller in the multi-area power system.

articleTitle: Formal Model of ATM Based on Object Constraint Language (OCL)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Formal methods (FM) are innovative methods which employ mathematical notations to specify explicit and precise requirements. This paper presents a formal model of an automated teller machine (ATM) using Object Constraint Language (OCL) to illustrate the benefits of employing FM to develop commercial applications. FM provide a mathematically rigorous framework for specifying, developing, and verifying software systems. It enhances reliability, robustness, and security. FM plays a crucial role in the context of ATM, which requires high levels of trust and correctness due to their financial and security-critical nature. Using OCL, we demonstrate how formal specifications can be applied to define an ATM system's precise behavior and constraints. It allows for the early detection and correction of errors, reducing development costs and improving overall system quality. This study argues that adopting FM in commercial applications not only boosts the reliability and security of the systems but also increases customer satisfaction and trust. Results of ATM development under OCL have been compared with traditional methods (TM), showing reductions such as 51 % in development time, 53 % in cost, 94 % in ambiguity and 97% in quality and customer trust.

articleTitle: Fabrication of the La0.9Sr0.1CrO3 Perovskite Nanoparticles as High-Performance Microwave Absorbers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: In this research, the fabrication of the La0.9Sr0.1 CrO3 perovskite nanoparticles (LSC NPs) through an efficient sol-gel method was reported. The prepared LSC NPs were characterized using X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) and field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM). The microwave absorption performance of the LSC NPs was evaluated by loading the perovskite nanoparticles fabricated at various calcination temperatures in a gum-based material as a green matrix. The maximum reflection loss <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{RL}_{\max})$</tex> of the LSC-700 NPs was -51.11 dB at 14.22 GHz in the thickness of 1.5 mm. articleTitle: Active User Detection in Massive MIMO Systems Using Compressed Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: In 5G and Beyond 5G wireless communication networks, Massive Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) technologies are essential for improved energy and spectrum efficiency. These kinds of systems are very effective at channel estimation and active user detection (AUD) in situations where there are many users and only a small percentage of them are sending data during a given time frame. Finding an active user is the biggest issue in this situation because it will have a direct effect on system performance. Sparsity in the user's activity pattern can be exploited through the use of Compressed Sensing (CS) techniques. Orthogonal Matching Pursuit with Iterative Refinement (OMP-IR) and Enhanced OMP (OMPe), two variants of the classic OMP algorithm, are the main subject of this study for compressed Sensing. By adding chaotic sequences, accuracy and robustness are increased and also the impact of noise and interreference is successfully reduced, leading to good accuracy in AUD. Details of Modeling has been shared in this paper which shows how angular sparsity has been exploited for AUD. Comparative visualization of different flavors of OMP is performed. Simulations show that enhanced version of OMP outperforms other flavor in AUD precision, which makes it more reliable for AUD in Massive MIMO systems. Which ultimately optimize resource allocation in high density user environment.

articleTitle: Implementation of Advanced Metering Infrastructure in the Indian Context with an Indigenous Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The implementation of indigenously developed Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) solutions for electricity utilities in the Indian context is explored in this work. The pilot deployment was carried out with the support of Kerala State Electricity Board Limited (KSEBL), and the project was funded by the National Mission on Power Electronics Technology (NaMPET) under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India. Implementing such a system came with its own set of challenges, from identifying suitable sites for meter deployment and gaining customer acceptance for smart meter technology to handling the complexities of heterogeneous communication interfaces. The project also required managing data from diverse meters in a structured format, finalizing detailed specifications, and ensuring seamless integration with existing billing systems through secure APIs. Additionally, implementing robust cybersecurity measures was critical to protect the integrity of the Meter Data Acquisition System (MDAS). Insights into these challenges and the solutions developed to address them are presented, providing valuable learnings for future AMI implementations.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Weight Differences of H0 and M4 Core Materials in Dry-Type Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This study examines the weight differences between two grades of cold-rolled grain-oriented (CRGO) electrical steel, H0 and M4, used in the manufacturing of transformer cores. By analyzing the core weight, this research aims to highlight the implications of material choice on the overall design and efficiency of transformers. The comparative analysis focuses on how the weight of H0 and M4 impacts the structural design, as well as the potential effects on performance and energy efficiency. The findings aim to provide valuable insights for decision-makers in the transformer design, enabling them to make informed choices regarding material selection based on weight considerations. Additionally, the study emphasizes the importance of optimizing core weight in relation to overall transformer design and functionality. Ultimately, this research aims to contribute to more efficient and effective transformer design through careful material selection. This study examines the design of a 2000 kVA transformer, ensuring that both core materials (H0 and M4) are manufactured for the same no-load losses.

articleTitle: Resource Optimization in Smart Cities: the Role of LoRaWAN Sensor Networks and Advanced Data Aggregation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The growing need for efficient data transmission in LoRaWAN-enabled smart city applications presents significant challenges in achieving timely response and precise monitoring, particularly in areas such as Smart Environmental Monitoring and Smart Waste Management. This study introduces a novel methodology, the Voronoi Aggregated Repli-code Squeeze Algorithm―to enhance transmission efficiency, facilitating early detection and rapid response. By integrating Voronoi-based spatial aggregation with Lempel-Ziv-Welch (LZW) compression, the proposed method effectively reduces data overhead and optimizes bandwidth utilization. This approach consolidates data from spatially distributed sensors into a single transmission packet, thereby reducing the frequency of individual transmissions, and compresses the aggregated data to further maximize efficiency. Simulation results indicate notable improvements in transmission rates, reduced latency, and enhanced resource management, making this approach highly suitable for data- dense urban environments.

Author Keywords: Smart Environmental Monitoring and Smart Waste Management

articleTitle: Regional Power Demand Forecasting Using BiLSTM and ConvBiLSTM Models for Sustainable Energy Management
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to develop an electricity demand forecasting model to improve the efficiency of energy management in specific regions. To achieve this, this study integrates various renewable energy sources and large-scale energy storage systems (ESS) to ensure the stability of the power grid. In this study, regional electricity demand forecasting is conducted using climate data (air temperature and ground temperature) for two major cities in Jeju Special Self-Governing Province of South Korea, Jeju-si and Seogwipo-si. Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM), and Convolutional BiLSTM (ConvBiLSTM) are used as forecasting models to compare their performance, and the forecasting performance of each model is evaluated to more accurately reflect the variability of electricity demand due to climate change. The performance results show that in Jeju-si, which has a relatively stable demand pattern, the model combining BiLSTM and ConvBiLSTM performs the best, enabling it to effectively learn the time dependencies and complex patterns. However, in Seogwipo-si, where demand volatility is comparatively high, the models performed relatively poorly, suggesting that more data and complex modelling approaches are needed. Consequently, this study highlights the potential of using deep learning models in renewable energy-based local power management, particularly for reducing power losses and increasing grid reliability through locally produced energy consumption.

articleTitle: Distributed Event-Based Secondary Control for Precise Reactive and Harmonic Power Sharing in Islanded AC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The proliferation of diverse loads in islanded AC Microgrids (MGs) poses a challenge for precise power sharing among Distributed Energy Resources (DERs). This article introduces a novel secondary control method utilizing a Distributed Event-Triggered Approach (DETA) designed for AC autonomous MGs. The DETA addresses circulating voltage drops across various loads, aiming to achieve accurate load sharing without requiring knowledge of mismatched feeder impedance. Incorporating time- and state-dependent threshold terms increases convergence rates while reducing the frequency of triggering events. Using Lyapunov stability analysis, parameters for the event-triggering function are determined and exclusion of Zeno behavior is proved. Extensive simulation results confirm the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Bayesian Synapse Driven by Quantum Hamiltonian and Electrical Interactions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: A probabilistic model of Synapse is proposed. In concrete, synapse is proposed as a Bayesian probability that requires the quantum probabilities for both: the interaction of Calcium 2+ in axon area, and the releasing of neurotransmitters. In this way, all available interactions that are carry out at axon zone, are dictated by quantum events. Once neurotransmitters are released from synaptic vesicles, their dynamics might be dictated by quantum probabilities based in a Hamiltonian. The diverse scenarios and their respective distribution of probabilities are simulated. From proposed theory, it is suggested that synapse would have a notable dependence on the accumulation of electric charges before and after the pass of neurotransmitters from a neuron to adjacent one. From the results, it is possible to argue that synapse is more than a biological phenomenon, a multidisciplinary event, that emphasizes the importance of transporting of electric charges with a potential dependence on probabilities, more than trivial determinism.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Mitigation Through Parasitic Structure in a Dual-Band Millimeter-Wave Flexible MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper introduces a dual-band millimeter-wave flexible multi-input multi-output (MIMO) antenna for wearable applications, comprising four identical elements in a cross configuration on a flexible Rogers RT5880 substrate. Each element includes a rectangular microstrip patch with an inverted U-shaped slot, facilitating dual-band operation at 28 GHz and 33 GHz. A parasitic structure was added to the MIMO design to reduce mutual coupling. Results indicate that the antenna achieves a bandwidth of 0.28 GHz (27.98-28.26 GHz) in the lower band and 1.01 GHz (32.24-33.25 GHz) in the upper band, with gains of 6.10 dBi at 28 GHz and 9.05 dBi at 33 GHz, and efficiencies of 0.77 and 0.88, respectively. The parasitic structure reduces the mutual coupling to below −20 dB across both bands. The antenna performed stably under extreme bending conditions. The low envelope correlation coefficient (< 0.05) and high diversity gain (approaching 10 dB) confirmed the effectiveness of MIMO communication. This dual-band MIMO antenna offers a promising solution for wearable applications with high isolation and stable performance.

articleTitle: A Single-Weight Neural Network for MIMO Signal Detection: Algorithm and Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Existing deep learning-based MIMO detectors often face substantial memory demands due to the need to store neural network weights, posing a significant challenge to practical implementation. To address this issue, we propose a single–weight neural network, namely SW–Net. By reducing each layer's weight vector to a scalar, the required hardware storage is significantly reduced. Simulation results demonstrate that hardware requirements can be reduced while maintaining bit error rate (BER) performance. Additionally, we present the corresponding VLSI hardware architecture, implemented using TSMC's 90–nm CMOS technology, operating at 707 MHz. This design requires 1109 kGEs and achieves a throughput of 707 Mbps.

articleTitle: Evaluating Key Performance Parameters of Hermetically Sealed Oil Transformers: A Study on Load Losses, No-Load Losses, and Leakage Impedance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper focuses on the design of hermetically sealed transformers. These transformers are produced in a controlled environment, significantly reducing the risk of moisture infiltration and contamination. The hermetic sealing process, which uses inert gases like nitrogen, minimizes the chances of moisture ingress and oxidation, ultimately extending the operational lifespan and reliability of the transformer. By employing analytical methods, this paper offers a comprehensive understanding of the essential design factors needed to create a robust, airtight transformer suitable for various harsh conditions. Key design aspects, including load losses, leakage inductance, and efficiency, are thoroughly examined in this study. Additionally, experimental tests are conducted to compare the results of the hermetically sealed transformer with traditional analytical methods, providing valuable insights into their performance.

articleTitle: An Architecture for Monitoring Elderly Using Digital Image Processing and Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The world population, on average, has seen its life expectancy increase. This phenomenon is causing the elderly population to grow. This reality has put pressure on the development of solutions - across a multidisciplinary spectrum - that are capable of helping the elderly in their daily lives. This assistance is especially important for elderly people who live alone and isolated - a common reality in many rural areas where there is a low population density. This work presents an architecture based on the use of digital image acquisition and processing associated with using Artificial Intelligence. This way, we can create solutions with easy deployment that do not disrupt the elderly's normal day-to-day life and ensure that third parties accompany them. Even though the proposed architecture can be complemented with sensory aspects linked to the elderly person themselves, this component, as it is independent and easily incorporated, was not the object of study.

articleTitle: Design Optimization of an Electric Motor for Improved Performance of a Battery-Powered Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The transition to battery-electric vehicles (BEVs) has increased the demand for efficient, cost-effective, and reliable electric motors. However, designing an electric motor that meets such criteria necessitates simultaneous consideration of many factors. Thus, it is beneficial to provide a basic understanding of electric motor fundamentals, highlight key design factors and methods regarding performance metrics, and explore novel technologies that can optimize future electric motors. Existing motor designs and novel applications of existing technology were reviewed to identify opportunities for improvement. This review demonstrated that modern electric motors have the potential for further efficiency optimization while remaining cost-effective. Furthermore, Finite Element Analysis (FEA) software was employed to reverse engineer the performance of three BEV Tesla motors, using available operating and physical data to determine their performance. The simulation results were within the performance error margin, indicating that FEA analysis of motor geometry via material data can accurately predict the performance and, therefore, design effectiveness per dollar of an electric motor. This research provides valuable insights into the fundamental design considerations for electric motors and offers promising avenues for future research and development in cost reduction and optimization.

articleTitle: Design of Signal Conditioner for Sensor Equipment of Human Body Surrogate for Forensic Crash Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper describes design and measurements of signal conditioner used for amplification of signals from accelerometers intended to use in human body surrogate for forensic crash testing. The design consists of instrumentation amplifier, Bessel low pass antialiasing filter and final gain stage. The characteristics of conditioner (frequency response, impulse response) are measured and compared with professional amplifier Endevco 136. Final testing of the conditioner together with sensor Endevco 7264H-2K is performed on the drop weight impact tester and the results are compared with Endevco 136, too.

articleTitle: Predictive Monitoring of Business Processes: A Case Study Using a Cumulative Fact Table Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Predictive Business Process Monitoring (BPPM) is an increasingly used technique to anticipate future events within organizations, based on the analysis of historical and real-time data. This article explores the application of a cumulative fact table model in a data warehouse to improve the accuracy and speed of predictions within the context of BPPM. Through a case study in the logistics sector, the proposed model significantly reduced the error rate in delivery time predictions and enabled faster anomaly detection compared to traditional methods. This approach has proven particularly effective for real-time monitoring of business processes, while also highlighting the need for a robust data infrastructure for its implementation.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling and Investigation of Streamer Breakdown in a Coaxial Plasma Torch Based on Townsend Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This article investigates electrical breakdown between the electrodes of a coaxial plasma burner for burning biogas. Simulations in COMSOL Multiphysics cover Townsend and streamer discharges in the air under normal conditions, focusing on electric field parameters, breakdown voltage, and electrode spacing. It was established that the breakdown occurs at a voltage of 13.5 kV, confirmed experimentally. The analysis showed that the streamer discharge develops faster than the Townsend discharge, demonstrating different ionization mechanisms. The results can be used to optimize plasma burners, increasing combustion stability and energy efficiency, which will contribute to developing plasma combustion technologies.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Indian Myna Trap*
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Indian Mynas adapt easily to urban environments, competing with native species and causing ecological, agricultural, and public health concerns. This project developed an AI-powered bird trap designed specifically to capture Indian Mynas while avoiding non-target species and maintaining self-sustainability through solar power. Integrating loT capabilities, the trap provides real-time updates to operators regarding its status, location, and security conditions, enhancing monitoring and operational control. Additionally, embedded AI technologies enhance detection accuracy, while loT capabilities provide real-time updates on the trap's status and location to operators. The system also includes security features to deter tampering, ensuring long-term reliability and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Approach to Accurately Model and Optimize Microwave Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Lately, Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) have been heavily used for radio frequency and microwave circuits and devices modelling. In this context, ANN based models are developed and assessed in this paper for the modelling and optimization of microwave filters. Four filter designs namely Low-Pass Filter (LPF), High-Pass Filter (HPF), Band-Pass Filter (BPF) and Band-Stop Filter (BSF) are developed and fabricated. The obtained S-parameters behaviors for a broad 0–10 GHz frequency spectrum are analyzed and simulated using ANNs. The developed models demonstrate excellent simulation accuracy, and regression score (R2) more than 99 % for all the filter designs,

articleTitle: Securing Data at Rest: Using ML-Driven Personally Identifiable Information(PII) Detection and Privacy-Preserving Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Modern Day Enterprises collect a vast amount of Personal Identifiable Information (PII) from different sources, including interactions with customers, online behavior, survey responses, user feedback, Internet of Things (loT) devices, smartphone usage, and activity on social networks. This information, which comes in structured, semi-structured, and unstructured formats, has been stored in sources like Databases, File shares, Data Lakes, Cloud storages, and Data warehouses hosted in Cloud and On-prem data centers. This data is crucial for tailoring decisions, offering businesses a competitive advantage, and delivering personalized experiences to stakeholders. However, with strict data protection laws like the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) in Europe, and Brazil's General Data Protection Law (LGPD) taking center stage, there's a pressing need for advanced methods to identify and secure PII that is stored at rest in On-Prem, Public cloud and SAAS systems. This study investigates Machine learning (ML), and artificial intelligence (AI) to find PII stored across different data formats automatically. Furthermore, it examines how encryption, anonymization and differential privacy can be applied to enhance the security of this data. These strategies ensure compliance with current data privacy laws and promote ethical data handling practices. The introduction of a comprehensive system that combines ML-based PII detection with these privacy-strengthening solutions offers a scalable, effective, and immediate way to address potential threats and enhance data safety. Simulations have proven this system's capability to significantly improve data security and reduce the risk of exposing sensitive information while it's at rest, thereby safeguarding the integrity of sensitive information.

articleTitle: Exploring Artificial Intelligence to Assist Kinematics Analysis of Rigid Bodies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence applications have spread to various areas of knowledge. Some of the applications of Machine Learning are Large Language Models and Natural Language Processing. An efficient way of communication between users and Artificial Intelligence information models is through Prompt Engineering. This article explores using Artificial Intelligence to assist in the kinematics analysis of rigid bodies through Prompt Engineering. The results obtained from the kinematic analysis of a Large Language Model are evaluated through a case study. Among the findings, it is determined that the results of the analysis depend on the clarity and content of details provided by the user in the creation of the Prompts used to make the queries, as well as the user's expertise in the subject of kinematic analysis of rigid bodies since it must be determined the certainty of the answers provided by Artificial Intelligence.

articleTitle: PaintBot: Autonomous Robotic Solution for Safe and Efficient Wall Painting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Indoor environments where people spend most of their time greatly benefit from aesthetic enhancements such as rich wall colors. However traditional wall painting methods are labor intensive, time consuming, and pose health risks due to the prolonged exposure to paint fumes along with the physical strain. These are common challenges that are faced in the construction industry. In this paper, the design and implementation of PaintBot, a cost effective, automated wall painting robot that enhances safety, reduces labor costs, and improves efficiency is presented. The proposed robot operates autonomously provided the dimensions and color specifications through the operator, initiating painting from an optimal starting point. PaintBot is equipped with actuators and a spray gun, and it maintains a precise distance from the wall to ensure uniform paint application. The resulting system provides a portable, simple, and efficient solution that produces professional quality wall finishes.

articleTitle: A Strategic Overview of 5G/6G Networks: Implications for 6G Security
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The imminent arrival of the sixth generation (6G) wireless communication technology necessitates a proactive approach to understanding and mitigating emerging cybersecurity risks. This paper offers a strategic analysis of 5G and 6G networks, highlighting critical vulnerabilities within the 6G ecosystem. Examining existing literature from 2020 to 2024, critical threats, including impersonation, privacy breaches, adversarial artificial intelligence (AI), and quantum attacks, are identified and mapped to specific 6G use cases. The mapped use cases include integrated sensing and communication, immersive communication, and hyper-reliable and low-latency communication (HRLLC). The study underscores the need for context-aware and adaptive security frameworks to safeguard the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of 6G networks.

articleTitle: Artificial Derivation of Schrödinger Equation Driven by Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Starting from the idea that artificial intelligent might be able to derive known as well as unknown equations of physics and other different branches of basic science, the concept of perceptron was used to derive the the well-known Schrödinger equation. The physics scenario has consisted in the case of a massive particle with an electric charge. While inputs have been defined as a family of polynomials dependent on the system energy, weights are characterized by having a direct dependence on unphysical variables. With this, wavefunction was reconstructed and it turned out to be the perceptron output. Also, Hamiltonian and evolution operator were reconstructed. The square of probability have displayed to exhibit up to two well-defined regions, situation that would come from perceptron methodology than derived from physics itself.

articleTitle: Secure Image Encryption U sing Dynamic Block Segmentation and Adaptive Pixel Modification with Chaotic Masking
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The widespread use of digital technologies has resulted in an increased generation, transmission and storage of digital images, which need to be secured effectively and efficiently. This paper proposes and evaluates a novel image encryption algorithm that comprises two secure components as its diffusion and confusion modules, i.e., a dynamic block segmentation and permutation module for diffusion and an adaptive pixel modification technique with chaotic masking for confusion. The dynamic block segmentation and permutation module divides the plain image in variable block sizes and then permutes the blocks randomly based on a chaotic permutation key. The adaptive pixel modification with chaotic masking module, on the other hand, obscures the pixel values of the permuted image in a cascaded manner, which ensures that the modification of one pixel affects all pixels within a block. Extensive security analysis validates the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm by exhibiting an entropy of 7.998 and a correlation value of 0.0004. These results indicate that proposed algorithm produces a cipher image with near-perfect entropy and almost zero correlation, making it highly resistant to cyberattacks.

articleTitle: Evaluating Object Tracking Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Object tracking is a critical task in computer vi-sion, with applications ranging from surveillance and human-computer interaction to augmented reality and medical imaging. This paper provides a comprehensive evaluation of various state-of-the-art object tracking algorithms, focusing on their performance in challenging scenarios such as occlusion, out-of-view conditions, and illumination variations. I examine six prominent algorithms: Struck, Deep Learning Tracker (DLT), Context Tracker (CXT), Adaptive Structural Local Sparse Ap-pearance Model (ASLA), Tracking-Learning-Detection (TLD), and Distribution Fields for Tracking (DFT). my study includes the collection of a diverse dataset from the internet to test these algorithms under realistic conditions. I highlight common issues such as overfitting to initial frames and target shifts during occlusion. By analyzing the performance of each algorithm on se-lected image sequences, I identify their strengths and weaknesses. Additionally, I propose success plots and average running time as key evaluation metrics, emphasizing the importance of both accuracy and real-time applicability in object tracking.

articleTitle: A Semantic-Driven Data Generative Traffic Modeling Method for Digital Twin Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Digital Twin Networks (DTN) create synchronized virtual replicas of physical networks to enable real-time monitoring, prediction, and optimization of network performance, facilitating efficient management in complex environments. However, existing DTN modeling often face challenges in accuracy, efficiency, and high communication costs. This paper proposes a novel semantic-driven traffic generation method that integrates diffusion models, network simulation, and semantic communication for constructing DTN. Our approach first extracts semantic information from real network data and inputs it into Mininet for initial traffic simulation. Then, to reduce discrepancies with real-world data, we introduce a Transformer-based diffusion model, DiffNTG, which refines Mininet-generated traffic to achieve high fidelity. Experimental results demonstrate that our model reduces error metrics between simulated and real networks by up to 96% and decreases computational costs by approximately 83%, showing strong potential for DTN applications.

articleTitle: From Classical to Quantum Energies of Harmonic Oscillator in a RC-Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper focuses on the energies of a quantum harmonic oscilaltor derived from a RC-circuit. The applied procedures have demanded to use the conversion from classical observables to quantum ones, through the usage of annihilator and creator operators. Once these operators have been solved, it is calculated the number of photons operator. Because these operations, the resulting quantum energies have turned out to be polynomial. The ground state is recovered in fully accordance to well-known quantum case. Some aspects inclined to quantum coherence in the context of quantum RC-circuit are presented.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Accelerated Real and Complex Multiple-Precision Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Sparse matrices have recently played a significant and impactful role in scientific computing, including artificial intelligence-related fields. According to historical studies on sparse matrix-vector multiplication (SpMV), Krylov subspace methods are particularly sensitive to the effects of round-off er-rors when using floating-point arithmetic. By employing multiple-precision linear computation, convergence can be stabilized by reducing these round-off errors. In this paper, we present the performance of our accelerated SpMV using SIMD instructions, demonstrating its effectiveness through various examples, including Krylov subspace methods.

articleTitle: Cloud SecN Avigator: RAG Approach to Bridge Gaps and Strengthen Cloud Security Practices with RAGAS Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: In recent years, many cyber incidents have resulted from misconfigurations of AWS. Although AWS provides exten-sive security guidelines, the sheer volume of documentation makes it difficult for developers to read and apply them completely. To address this, we propose a development support tool, Cloud SecNavigator. This tool uses Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to extract relevant content and accurately respond to user queries based on AWS documentation. Our evaluation measures Cloud SecNavigator's output accuracy using two approaches: (1) Retrieval-Augmented Generation Assessment (RAGAS) and (2) a comparative accuracy assessment between Cloud SecNavigator-generated responses and a non-RAG LLM (GPT-40). The results indicate that Cloud Sec-Navigator achieves superior accuracy, highlighting its potential as an effective development support tool.

articleTitle: Optimized Low-Noise Amplifier with Switchable Carrier Aggregation Mode for LTE-Advanced and 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Carrier aggregation, especially intra-band, could suffer from receiver desensitization due to the existence of intermodulation distortions in the bands of operation of the low-noise amplifier and/or the presence out-of-band jammer signals. Highly linear components are needed to reject these interferences. This configuration can work switchably between legacy and CA mode with minimal degradation in its linearity using load disconnection. It achieved steady 14.2dB gain (S21 and S31) in both legacy and CA mode. The noise performance variation is recorded to be 0.1dB, as the topology achieved a 1.53dB and 1.52dB of NF in legacy and CA modes, respectively. The integration of the derivative superposition method enabled the CA LNA to achieve linearity levels fit for carrier aggregation application. In all interference scenarios, the IIP3 is greater than +10dBm. Specifically, it achieved +16.9dBm and +16.5dBm of in - band IIP3 in CA and legacy modes, respectively. While in OOB linearity analysis, it achieved a +14.5dBm and +14.4dBm IIP3 value in CA and legacy modes. The proposed architecture is designed using the RF library of TSMC 65-nm CMOS technology and is tested at Long-Term Evolution (LTE) band 2. This scheme utilized the lay-out of an on-chip low-density standard spiral inductor. It also includes an ultra-thick top metal layer that has been used as the major routing metal to reduce parasitic resistances. The chip layout has an area of 0.9085mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Hamiltonian-based Quantum Paths Guided by Engineered Perceptron
