publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The case of a massive particle traveling along the space-plane but guided by an algorithm based at perceptron, is presented. Essentially, it is defined the corresponding Hamiltonian that in a first instance turns out to be for free particle. However, the presence of disturbs suggest to employ additional terms to Hamiltonian in according to perceptron topology. In this manner, the activation function is focused on the expended energy from a point to next. The space-time transitions are canceled when disturbs are big enough that particle's trajectory if fully disturbed so that probability that final point is reached is small. Only when perceptron is adequate to every space-point, algorithm can guarantee the arrival of particle for all available quantum states.

articleTitle: An Efficient Predictive Spectrum Allocation Algorithm for Multi-User Cognitive Radio IoT Devices Within GSM900 Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: IoT, fifth generation and multiple new wireless systems are growing up rapidly and spectrum resource is being congested continuously. Therefore, an efficient spectrum allocation strategy should be taken place to tackle this serious situation. This work presents a predictive spectrum allocation algorithm designed to enhance the transmission performance of cognitive radio Internet of Things (CR-IoT) devices operating within the GSM900 band. Our proposed system combines spectrum prediction and sharing to identify and allocate unused frequency channels efficiently. This dual-process approach optimizes channel access for cognitive users (CUs), maximizing transmission duration and bandwidth sharing while minimizing the need for spectrum handoffs (SHOs). The algorithm is evaluated using three key performance metrics: “Throughput in time-domain”, “Throughput in frequency-domain”, and “Spectrum Handover rate” (SHO) (for QoS enhancing and latency decreasing). Results indicate that the proposed allocation algorithm achieved a global TAR of 78.47%, a maximum allocation rate of more than 96.8% of available channels for 2158 simultaneously accessed CUs, a high interference avoidance rate (IAR) of 94,5% in frequency-domain, and a low SHO rate of approximately 0.19%, highlighting its effectiveness in supporting seamless and robust spectrum access for multi-user CR-IoT applications without interfering with licensed users.

articleTitle: Architecture for Efficient Food Management and Waste Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This article presents a modular architecture for developing the ZeroWaste mobile application, designed to optimize food management in the home environment and reduce food waste through collaborative and scalable features. Food waste is a global issue with severe environmental, economic, and social repercussions, and ZeroWaste seeks to address this challenge by promoting conscious and sustainable consumption practices. Developed in React Native to support multiple platforms, the application integrates Firebase for authentication, notifications, and real-time data storage, enabling timely alerts on product expiration and facilitating user control over food inventory. Additionally, it incorporates an artificial intelligence module that suggests personalized recipes based on available products, encouraging food usage before spoilage. The proposed architecture also includes an automated product registration system using barcode scanning, supporting the creation of a community database that streamlines food item identification. Other features, such as shared shopping lists and multi-residence inventory management, expand the collaborative scope of the application, fostering the exchange and donation of food between users. With its flexible and expandable design, ZeroWaste is oriented towards continuous development and future improvements, meeting the growing need for technological solutions in sustainable and collaborative food management. This architectural proposal provides a robust foundation for developing an innovative solution.

articleTitle: Recreate Immersive Scenarios for Practicing Sports in Gyms - User Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a mobile application to integrate immersive features into fitness devices to enhance user experience and athletic performance. The proposed architecture ensures compatibility with a wide range of fitness equipment, regardless of brand or model. Central to the system is the playback of authentic route videos, augmented by contextual data such as speed, altitude, and environmental conditions. This allows dynamic equipment control, adjusting parameters like resistance and slope for a more consistent immersive experience. The application acts as a central interface, managing video recordings and data collection, all synchronized through a cloud-based platform that builds a community-driven repository of shared routes. Additionally, the application integrates cloud and edge computing alongside artificial intelligence to provide tailored workout adjustments based on historical performance and real-time metrics. Communication between the application, fitness devices, and wearables relies on SIG BLE standards. Users can create new immersive routes and download shared ones for enhanced training sessions. The paper elaborates on the application's architectural design and technological choices while discussing implementation progress, challenges, and future improvements.

articleTitle: Adaptive Sliding Mode Control for a Blower-Based Breathing Simulator with Unknown and Time-Varying Airway Resistance and Compliance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Looking back at history, the world has experienced many pandemics that affect the people experiencing respiratory system, and most recently, the severe devastation of the COVID-19 pandemic. This reflects the reality of life and the global disparity in ventilator availability between high-income countries and low and middle-income countries. Additionally, various simple ventilators and breathing simulators are non-functional with various artificial lungs due to dynamic lung parameter changes during operation. Therefore, this paper proposes an adaptive controller for a novel blower-based breathing simulator to address the challenge of unknown and varying artificial lung parameters. Specifically, an adaptive sliding mode controller has been developed for precise volume control under uncertain conditions. Alongside that, the metric Integral of Absolute Error (IAE) is used to evaluate control performance. The first simulation scenario with three different input signals, which comprise a ramp, parabolic, and sinusoidal, remained permissible errors below 5%. In the other scenario, the blower-based breathing simulator model's control performance with two different airway parameters sets IAE values over 12 cycles. In the 6 initial cycles, the trend of IAE values shows a gradual decrease over cycles. At cycle 7, a change in airway parameters causes a difference in the IAE value, but it quickly decreases in the following cycles. As indicated by this outcome, the proposed controller proves not only efficient when the airway parameters are unknown constants but also adaptable when these parameters change over time.

articleTitle: Attention-Driven Feature Fusion Integrating Swin Transformer and CNN Models for Improved Ocular Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Fundus images are crucial for diagnosing ocular diseases, but timely and accurate classification remains chal-lenging due to complex retinal structures and significant class imbalances in datasets like the Ocular Disease Intelligent Recog-nition (ODIR). In this paper, we present a hybrid deep learning model that synergizes the Swin Transformer, Inception V3, and EfficientNetBO architectures to enhance ocular disease classi-fication. We improve multi-scale feature extraction by adding dilated convolutions to the Swin Transformer and integrating global average pooling into the Inception V3 and EfficientN etBO models. After these modifications, we unfreeze the last few layers of each model and fine-tune them on the ODIR dataset, which we partitioned into 80 % for training and 20 % for testing. We then concatenate the outputs and apply a self-attention mechanism to focus on the most informative features. To address the inherent class imbalance in the ODIR dataset, we use class-specific weights and employ focal loss during training, which alleviates the model's sensitivity to underrepresented classes and improves recall for these categories. Our model demonstrates superior performance across all eight ocular disease categories, achieving an average precision and recall of 90 %, with values ranging from 84% to 98%. Notably, it attains precision and recall of 98% for cataract detection and 96 % for myopia. These results underscore the effectiveness of combining convolutional neural networks and transformer architectures with attention-based feature fusion for comprehensive ocular disease classification.

articleTitle: Enhancing Video Projector Connectivity and Management with a Low-Cost Solution
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The video projector serves as an essential device for various purposes, such as education, corporate functions, and conferences. This article presents an affordable setup aimed at upgrading video projection equipment, including older models, with enhanced management and sharing features. The proposed solution tackles frequent connectivity challenges arising from dif-ferences in connectors, transmission methods, and mismatches in configurations (like frequency and resolution) between computers and projectors. Such incompatibilities often result in delays and hinder the effective use of video projectors. By incorporating a Raspberry Pi and three dedicated applications, this system introduces an intuitive solution that supports innovative teaching and work methods.

articleTitle: Development of Low Cost “Epi -seizure” Device for the Prediction and Detection of Tonic-Clonic Seizures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Epilepsy is ranked internationally as the fourth most common neurological disorder that affects around 80% of low to middle-income countries' population. Generalized tonic-clonic seizures are the most severe form of epileptic seizures. They are by far the most dreaded seizure kind amongst patients, family, and spectators, and are generally connected with total unconsciousness or reduced awareness. Early detection of the disease is critical in order to prevent seizure symptoms from occurring. Although various antiepileptic medications are available, effective monitoring of the disorder is often unattainable. This is because the existing devices are of high cost, unportable, and most of them are used only for detection purposes. To overcome these limitations, this project aims to design a real-time, algorithm based on biosignals analysis using electrodermal activity and respiratory rate sensors. It is an integration of a low-cost, non-invasive, portable device that could be worn either under patient's clothes, or on the wrist around the clock. The proposed device is not limited to monitoring seizure symptoms but also predicts seizure occurrences to help caregivers during the monitoring process. After testing the sensors on collected data with 25 subjects, it was proved that the algorithm used to predict and detect seizure occurrence is entirely reliant on phasic readings. The data will then be sent using telemedicine technology through a developed application. The Epi-seizure device has the potential to significantly improve the quality of life for individuals with epilepsy by enabling proactive management of seizures and reducing associated risks. Future work will focus on larger-scale testing and refining the algorithm for even greater accuracy.

articleTitle: Fatigue Detection of Drivers Using Image Processing and Artificial Intelligence Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Road traffic accidents pose a serious threat to public safety and are a major source of fatalities around the world, particularly those brought on by driver drowsiness. With the development of artificial intelligence (AI), efforts have been made to create innovative projects and systems targeted at identifying driver weariness and issuing early warnings. In this study, we describe a real-time driver detection and warning system that makes use of deep artificial intelligence, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), open CV face recognition, and image processing methods. CNNs can recognize small changes in a driver's behavior or appearance that suggest fatigue because they perfectly replicate the human visual systems. These networks are highly accurate in identifying patterns and signs of fatigue because they have been trained on huge datasets of driving behavior. The CNNs are integrated into a system that continuously analyzes the behavior of the driver using a variety of sensors, including cameras and biometric sensors, to identify indicators of fatigue, such as drooping eyelids, and notify the driver through tactile, visual, or audio messages. By creating a cutting-edge AI system that accurately identifies driver fatigue and swiftly alerts other drivers, the research potentially prevents accidents and saves lives on the road.

Index Terms: ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge

articleTitle: The Influence of Kanban Agile Methodology on Software Project Management: A Survey Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Software project management (SPM) is an important process in the software development (SD) industry, that involves the planning, organizing, and overseeing software application development. Kanban agile (KA) methodology is a systematic project management approach that prioritizes workflow optimization, clear visibility, and continuous delivery in SD. It has become increasingly popular in software development for its ability to adapt to changing requirements and promote continuous delivery. It is examined that kanban affects critical project management factors. Data is gathered through a survey of software professionals who are experienced with kanban. The results indicate that kanban significantly improves team collaboration, workflow transparency, and overall project efficiency. This study investigates the impact of the KA methodology on SPM using a survey-based approach. However, the study also identifies challenges, including the initial learning curve and resistance to change within teams. These findings provide valuable insights for organizations considering kanban and contribute to the broader understanding of its role in SPM. We surveyed several software development companies, and the results show that almost all of them use agile methodology (Kanban), which improves SPM as compared to other agile methodologies like Scrum, extreme programming and dynamic systems development methods.

articleTitle: Enhancing Power System Protection with Machine Learning: A Smart and Reliable Approach for Insulator Inspection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Increasing demand for electricity due to technological advancement in every aspect of human life has increased the importance of the smooth operation of distribution lines. Distribution lines pass through mountains, deserts, forests and many other inaccessible zones. Therefore, the detection of present and future hazards to transmission lines due to the presence of anything on the line, human towns adjacent to the distribution lines, trees of forests, new plants nearer to the lines, and birds nest is an important concern. Conventionally, these lines were inspected by line men which consumes too much time, increases inspection cost because of the huge workforce, increases human life and safety risks, compromises the reliability of the data and take too much delay in the desired information. In order to cope with the aforementioned problems, an unmanned autonomous vehicle (UAV) is proposed in this study with an instant camera is proposed for distribution lines insulator inspection. This system can monitor the physical conditions of the insulator. This UAV-based system is capable to replace humans which reduces workforce costs and increases human life security and data reliability. In this study, a technician or any other expert maintains a distance and operates UAV to observe the lines. Further Machine Learning-Based algorithms help in fault classifications. It's an easy, safe, and long-lasting way to analyze transmission and distribution lines. In the local market of Pakistan, the proposed system of inspection and fault detection through imaging of distribution lines can be used by WAPDA and all DISCOs (distribution companies). It can inspect distribution lines that are unreachable where manual labor cannot inspect.

articleTitle: Recursive Least Squares Algorithm for Online Parameter Identification of DC Motor: Theory and Practice
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: In the automation era, DC motors are widely utilized across various industries due to their adaptability and efficiency. In the downside of reality, accurately modelling and controlling their behavior under diverse operational conditions remains challenging. Hence, this study proposes a comprehensive approach integrating Recursive Least Squares (RLS) for parameter estimation within ARX models, combined with experiment data to enhance model accuracy. Moreover, State Feedback Control is applied to optimize DC motor operation. Specifically, the model coefficients are predicted over time, alongside recording the error between the actual output and predicted output within a 30 -second timeframe. The results indicate that the error is controlled and converges to 0 within 0.5-second (approximately 10 cycles). As a result, in the online model updates, system error increases and deviates from zero over time due to model drift, likely caused by environmental factors or changes in the motor's temperature. In contrast, the error remains stabilized around zero with online model updates, demonstrating improved control effectiveness through continuous model adaptation.

articleTitle: Enhancing Forensic Audio Transcription with Neural Network-Based Speaker Diarization and Gender Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Forensic audio transcription is often compromised by low-quality recordings, where indistinct speech can hinder the accuracy of conventional Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems. This study addresses this limitation by developing a machine learning-based approach to improve speaker diarization, a process critical for distinguishing between speakers in sensitive audio data. Previous research highlights the inadequacy of traditional ASR in forensic settings, particularly where audio quality is poor and speaker overlap is common. This paper presents a neural network specifically designed for gender classification, using 20 key acoustic features extracted from real forensic audio data. The model architecture includes input, hidden, and output layers tailored to differentiate male and female voices, with dropout regularization to prevent overfitting and hyperparameter optimization ensuring robust generalization across test data. The neural network achieved an average recall of 86.81%, F1 score of 85.67%, precision of 87.95%, and accuracy of 86.83% across varied audio conditions. This model significantly improves transcription accuracy, reducing errors in legal contexts and supporting judicial processes with more reliable, interpretable evidence from sensitive audio data.

articleTitle: Automatic Parsing and Extraction of Structured Data from Fax Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper presents a sophisticated system designed to automatically convert fax images into structured, formatted data. The system employs a multi-stage approach to enhance accuracy and efficiency. Initially, faxes are classified into predefined categories to match their functional layouts, which allows the application of specialized data extraction models for different fax types. This pre-processing step enables the extraction models to focus on specific document styles, improving overall accuracy. The system utilizes GoogleNet for classification, achieving a high accuracy rate of 100%. For the data extraction process, the paper details two primary tasks: detecting text snippets and table cells, and recognizing these texts using Optical Character Recognition (OCR). The Light-Head R-CNN object detection model, combined with ResNet-101, is employed to effectively identify table cells and text regions. For text recognition, a Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network (CRNN) is used, incorporating VGG- 16 as the CNN backbone and a bi-directional LSTM with a CTC output layer for sequential character generation. The paper also introduces an incremental learning strategy utilizing author feedback to continuously refine the models. This approach, based on knowledge distillation, ensures the system adapts to new data without forgetting previously learned information. Future work will focus on improving the conversion of tabular data and addressing the variability in document layouts across different companies.

articleTitle: Powering the Future of Urban Air Mobility: Electrical Design and Systems in eVTOL Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The integration of electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft into urban air mobility environments has the potential to reduce traffic congestion in densely populated metropolitan areas. eVTOLs combine the capabilities of helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft, making them ideal for short-to medium-distance urban travels. This paper discusses the electrical design, power systems, and control architectures of eVTOLs with prospects for efficient, sustainable, and scalable aerial transportation within smart cities. Hybrid-electric and full-electric propulsion are the focus of the airline industry to achieve sustainability in smart cities. eVTOLs are among the most promising solutions for congestion, pollution, and urban accessibility. Wingless, lift+cruise, and vectored thrust eVTOL configurations are discussed and compared to provide a comprehensive analysis of their performance and application areas, from short-range air taxis to regional shuttles. Furthermore, this paper discusses the classification, powertrain, power sources, and control systems of eVTOLs. It also highlights Dubai's proactive attempt to integrate autonomous flying vehicles with major challenges from the regulatory, operational, and infrastructural perspectives. This analysis provides insight into recent technological advancements, design considerations, and the possible impact of eVTOLs on urban mobility systems, leading to a sustainable and time-efficient alternative to traditional ground-based transportation.

articleTitle: Aerobic Athletes Tracking System Using Smart Glove for Physiological and Kinematic Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a novel Smart Glove designed specifically for aerobic athletes, enabling real-time monitoring of physiological parameters, including heart rate, SpO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and body temperature, alongside kinematic data such as speed and distance. Existing wearable devices often lack the combination of accuracy, ergonomics, and cost-effectiveness required for dynamic sports environments. By positioning the primary sensors at the fingertip, this design enhances measurement reliability without restricting movement. The glove incorporates data interpretation, providing actionable feedback via a mobile interface. Methodology, experimental results, and key findings demonstrate the efficacy and usability of this solution.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of LIME and Shape Analysis Techniques in Prostate Cancer MRI Interpretation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) are enabling the integration of explainable AI (XAI) models in Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) to improve diagnostic accuracy and personalize prostate cancer treatment. This paper explores the effectiveness of two XAI techniques, Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) and shape analysis, in interpreting prostate cancer MRI datasets. A central focus is the necessary validation to ensure these models provide reliable and actionable diagnostic insights. However, the persistent “black-box problem,” which refers to the lack of transparency and interpretability in AI decision-making, has led to clinical skepticism regarding deep learning applications. Since most AI models produce results without clearly explaining their internal processes, radiologists may need help understanding the rationale behind predictions, limiting AI's role as a decision-support tool. In this study, we stress the need for validation to ensure that XAI-generated explanations are reliable and clinically useful. Their findings are intended to help integrate XAI into clinical practice and aid in transforming AI from an opaquer to a more transparent and crucial aid to radiologists in diagnosing and managing prostate cancer.

articleTitle: Improving Data Center Operational Reliability and Energy Efficiency Through Hot-Standby based ITE Cooling System Redundancy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: In modern data centers, cooling systems for IT equipment (ITE) play a vital role in maintaining continuous operation and promptly adapting to fluctuations in IT service demands. This research introduces a hot standby sparing (HSP)- based cooling system that enhances redundancy while maximizing energy efficiency, particularly for data centers that demand N+1 or higher redundancy to ensure reliable, uninterrupted performance. Redundancy strategies in data centers are generally categorized into hot standby (HSP), warm standby (WSP), and cold standby (CSP). For facilities equipped with variable speed drive (VSD) or variable frequency drive (VFD) technologies and requiring N+1 or greater redundancy, HSP-based cooling is recommended for superior energy optimization. A case study conducted on a large-scale, 30 MW-class A-Data Center compared the energy performance of CSP and HSP cooling systems. Findings revealed that the HSP-based system reduced cooling power consumption by approximately 15% compared to the CSP-based alternative, while achieving a power usage effectiveness (PUE) of 1.20. These results highlight the HSP approach as the most effective solution for significantly improving energy efficiency in cooling operations without necessitating substantial upgrades or additional investments in infrastructure.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cryptographic Security in RTOS: Addressing Vulnerabilities in Embedded Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper systematically reviews the cryptographic methods utilized in embedded systems Real-Time Operating Systems (RTOS), highlighting significant threats that must be addressed immediately. This urgency is raised due to these methodologies' effective aid in the preservation of confidential information, protecting the system, and providing an offense against external attacks. This study presents an overview of the existing security protocols dedicated to RTOS with regard to its historical developments and evaluates the use of methods and systems of proper cryptography. As a result of the systematic understanding of the core problems, common vulnerabilities are revealed and new approaches to strengthening these systems are put forward. Structural and functional characteristics of the proposed solutions are tested under the implementation of the RTOS security, covering plausible defense mechanisms in light of the increase in computer-based attacks. This paper paves the way for future research endeavors to fill in the gaps by proposing or implementing dynamic security strategies.

articleTitle: A Verifiable Framework using Trusted Execution Environments for Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Machine learning is now widespread and utilized across various industries for mission-critical applications such as fraud detection, algorithmic trading, and predicting disease-spreading patterns. Machine learning models require rich data for training, processing input, and inference. Importantly, all these services are now deployed in third-party public clouds, where consumers have little choice but to place implicit trust in the cloud provider to protect the confidentiality of their data without any validation. This inevitably poses security and privacy challenges, including issues related to various regulatory and legal requirements such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA). To address this, we propose a verifiable PPML framework using TEE that will address various privacy threats to Machine Learning as a Service (MLaaS). Our framework enables MLaaS providers to deliver their use cases seamlessly without requiring changes to their Machine Learning (ML) model or training data while providing verifiable trust to enterprises. We demonstrate the framework through a public cloud proof of concept (POC).

articleTitle: Classifying Malicious Insider Threats Based On User Activity and Behavioral Profile Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Detecting malicious insider threats is a critical concern for organizations due to the potential for significant damage and the subtle nature of such activities. Insider threats are inherently complex to identify because malicious actions often masquerade as legitimate behavior, making traditional detection methods insufficient. Current approaches frequently rely on limited data sources and fail to capture the multifaceted aspects of user behavior, leading to gaps in threat detection. In this paper, we propose a novel methodology that addresses these challenges by integrating advanced natural language processing techniques, statistical feature analysis, and psychometric profiling. We lever-age textual content from user communications and web activities, apply statistical analyses on temporal and frequency-based be-havioral data, and incorporate users' psychometric profiles based on OCEAN scores to create comprehensive behavioral profiles. An isolation forest model is utilized as an anomaly detector to identify malicious activities and the users responsible. Our iterative approach assesses the contribution of each data source to detection efficacy, and we employ dimensionality reduction techniques to refine feature importance. Experimental results demonstrate that our integrated model significantly outperforms existing methods, effectively enhancing the detection of malicious insider activities by addressing the limitations of current approaches.

articleTitle: Semi-supervised Segmentation-driven Classification Pipeline for Grading Cassava Leaf Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Cassava, a vital food security crop widely cultivated in tropical regions, serves as a major carbohydrate source globally. However, its growth and productivity are consistently hindered by the prevalence of viral, bacterial, and fungal diseases. This paper introduces a novel semi-supervised segmentation-driven classification framework designed to identify cassava leaf diseases with high precision. Utilizing a modified Color Index Vegetation Extraction (CIVE) technique, our framework generates pixel-level pseudo labels that facilitate the training of a segmentation unit without the need for densely annotated data. This semi-supervised approach significantly reduces the reliance on extensive human-annotated resources and effectively segments cassava leaves from complex backgrounds, enabling accurate classification of four major cassava diseases: cassava mosaic disease (CMD), cassava bacterial blight (CBB), cassava brown streak disease (CBSD), and cassava green mottle (CGM). The proposed framework is validated on the publicly available Kaggle Cassava 2019 dataset, on which it outperforms the state-of-the-art works by 7.69%, 8.98%, and 7.77% in terms of precision, recall, and F1 score, respectively. Additionally, it yielded a mean accuracy of 89.73% and an F1 score of 0.89 on the Cassava Leaf Disease 2020 dataset.

articleTitle: Migraine Classification from EEG Signals Using ML Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Migraine is a complex neurological disorder with symptoms that often overlap with other conditions, complicating accurate diagnosis. This study applies machine learning (ML) for migraine classification using EEG data to improve diagnostic ac-curacy. EEG recordings from 36 subjects (healthy and migraine-affected) were processed to extract significant features through band-pass filtering, Independent Component Analysis (ICA), and Power Spectral Density (PSD) analysis. Two neural network models, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Deep Neural Networks (DNN), were trained on these features, with CNN achieving 97% accuracy. These findings highlight the potential of EEG-based ML in reliable migraine classification, paving the way for practical clinical applications.

articleTitle: Addressing Class Imbalance in X-ray Threat Detection with Self-Supervised Balanced DINO
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Aviation security, which is mainly tasked with the assurance of safety to the travelers by offering reliable baggage screening, remains a very critical issue. Traditional manual inspections are prone to errors and labor intensive. This calls for automatic detection systems. However, methods commonly used for X-ray threat detection have the problem of data imbalance and poor feature representation, especially for rare threat items. It proposes a novel Balanced DINO framework that incorporates the Focal-Augmented Loss to tackle the above challenges into a DINO-based Vision Transformer. Our study aims at balancing class representations, using both algorithmic weighting and data augmentation methods, to improve the detection accuracy of the rare threat items. Balanced DINO demonstrates extensive testing on three public datasets, namely SIXray, CLCXray, and COMPASS-XP, with considerably improved performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. Concrete, our framework outperforms the competitors by at most 3.77% in F1-score and at most 2.31% in accuracy on the highly imbalanced SIXray dataset, which firmly proves that our framework is robust and adaptable for different settings,

articleTitle: Navigating Adverse Weather: An Exploration of YOLOv8's Object Detection in Fog
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Object detection in adverse weather conditions, such as dense fog, poses a critical challenge for computer vision systems in applications like autonomous driving, surveillance, and robotics. Image quality degradation due to light scattering and absorption diminishes the performance of even the most advanced models trained on clear-weather datasets. This paper uses the Foggy Cityscapes dataset to evaluate YOLOv8, a cutting-edge object detection model, under extreme foggy conditions. We utilize YOLOv8's sophisticated architecture, featuring the CSPDarknet backbone and Path Aggregation Network (PANet), for efficient feature extraction and multi-scale detection. Our approach incorporates image enhancement techniques and data augmentation to mitigate the effects of fog on feature visibility. We conduct a comprehensive performance assessment using metrics like mean average precision (mAP) precision-recall curves to evaluate the model's robustness and reliability. Additionally, we benchmark YOLOv8 against previous YOLO versions, detailing improvements and trade-offs in detection speed and accuracy. We also propose a hybrid framework combining multi-task learning to improve image quality and object detection in low-visibility scenarios.

articleTitle: Analysis of Ceilometer LiDAR(CL51) Sensor Atmospheric Profile Images for Urban Environmental Monitoring Over Pretoria, South Africa
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Clouds are a critical component of the atmosphere, influencing both climate and weather patterns, while their backscatter impacts human activities and lives. The CL 51 Ceilometer LiDAR is one of the advanced atmospheric sensors deployed globally to collect massive data for monitoring environmental conditions. This sensor captures data in digital format, which is subsequently converted into images. However, extracting atmospheric features, such as aerosol distribution along the sensor's path length, requires precise identification for effective analysis. In this paper, we outline the methodology for data acquisition, conversion to image format, and feature extraction of atmospheric components from the CL 51 script. We further analyse the atmospheric images derived from CL 51 seasonal data collected in Pretoria from 2014 to 2015. This analysis of CL 51 ceilometer LiDAR images will enhance our knowledge and understanding of the atmospheric aerosol profile, thereby contributing to urban environmental monitoring efforts.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Framework for Digital Experimental Reports: Integrating Chaoxing Platform in Experimental Education
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The traditional approach to experimental teaching often involves cumbersome, paper-based reporting, which can be time-consuming, repetitive, and lacks the interactive qualities necessary for engaging students effectively. This paper presents a novel approach to digitalizing university physics experimental reports using the Chaoxing Learning Platform. By integrating digital components into the experimental reporting process, this study aims to streamline experimental documentation, improve student engagement, and enhance the overall quality of experimental education. The proposed design includes a three-part structure comprising a Pre-Experiment Report, an Experiment Record Page, and a Post-Experiment Summary Report. The methodology is based on constructivist learning theory, Outcome-Based Education (OBE), and the BOPPPS model (Bridge-in, Objective, Pre-assessment, Participatory Learning, Post-assessment, Summary) to provide a comprehensive framework that supports student-centered learning. The results demonstrate the potential benefits of this approach in improving learning outcomes, enhancing digital literacy, and fostering active participation. This study concludes by discussing the broader implications of digital integration in experimental education and proposing future research directions, including the potential scalability of the approach to other experimental sciences.

articleTitle: MUS490: Advanced Feature Selection and Unsupervised Clustering for Music Categorization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper presents MUS490, an innovative tool for the automated clustering and categorization of music files using unsupervised machine learning techniques. MUS490 leverages Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), Onset-Based Spectral Information (OBSI), and Amplitude Modulation (AM) features to analyze timbre, genre, and instrumental characteristics of music datasets. The tool's primary contributions include the implementation of auto-k and auto-weight algorithms within the K-means framework, enabling dynamic determination of cluster counts and feature significance. Through a series of tests on diverse datasets, MUS490 demonstrates its capability to partition music into intuitive and sometimes unexpected categories, such as instrument type, genre, and tempo. While successful in many respects, the system's performance highlights challenges related to outlier detection and cluster precision, particularly in heterogeneous datasets. Future work aims to address these issues through improved heuristics, parallel processing, and integration of alternative clustering algorithms like DBSCAN. MUS490 represents a significant step towards fully automated music classification, with potential applications in music analysis, recommendation systems, and genre discovery.

articleTitle: An Overview on Switching to Renewable Energy Resources in Pakistan for Sustainable Future: Its Challenges and Policy Recommendations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Pakistan's heavy reliance on energy imports has a dominant negative effect on its economic growth. This has resulted in increase in import bills. In this paper, a review has been made of the negative impacts of petroleum imports on Pakistan's economy and the environment. The potential of renewable energy sources (RES) has been exploited to mitigate these effects. The paper further explores the potential of RES such as wind, solar, and hydroelectric power to mitigate these effects and promote sustainable economic growth. The case study of Costa Rica, which has successfully transitioned to renewable energy, has also been discussed. The review finds that the high cost of petroleum imports leads to a trade deficit, inflation, budget deficit, and environmental degradation which can be managed by integration of renewable energy resources into the system hence reducing Pakistan's dependency on imported fuels.

articleTitle: Enhanced Vision Aid for Low Vision Tertiary Students
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Education is one of the essential contributors to development in society. Unlike informal education that can be carried out in many forms, formal education requires structured learning processes. Unfortunately, low vision students find it difficult to fit into these structures in tertiary institutions. This is because they need extra aid to manage the numerous tasks in school. The existing aids for these students are expensive and discourages most of them from pursuing higher education. To solve this problem, we present a Realtek AMB82-based, battery powered, low-cost, and portable live streaming aid to help these students read content being shared during class lectures. The video was shot with the JXF37 1080p resolution camera having a 30-fps frame rate. The video stream was transmitted over Wi-Fi with a chunked transfer encoding technique over HTTP. A user interface was designed using basic HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to view and apply preferred image enhancement filters to support reading. This device was able to help a low vision student read contents about three meters far from the whiteboard. The device has close to no running costs and is thus a sustainable product for society. By introducing this to many universities we can increase the number of low vision students that access higher education.

articleTitle: Injectable Applications: Enhancing Privacy and Security in Web Interactions through Priv.ly
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper introduces Priv.ly, a novel web privacy architecture that enables the injection of privacy-preserving applications, termed Injectable-Apps, into untrusted web platforms. Priv.ly decouples content from host platforms by using C-Servers to store and manage data, ensuring that sensitive information is protected from unauthorized access. Injectable- Apps leverage various cryptographic techniques, including symmetric and public key cryptography, to safeguard user data across different communication channels. The architecture also addresses potential security threats such as spoofing, content tracking, and distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks by implementing robust mitigation strategies. By allowing users to manage their cryptographic identities and control key distribution, Priv.ly empowers them to protect their privacy in a flexible and user-friendly manner. This paper discusses the design principles, security implications, and potential use cases of Priv.ly, highlighting its ability to integrate seamlessly with existing social networks and web applications.

articleTitle: Scaling Unicyclic Graph Analysis: Automated Generation, Augmentation, and Machine Learning-Driven Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Unicyclic graphs featuring a single cycle within a connected structure are crucial in modeling chemistry, biology, and information science networks. Traditional analysis methods, reliant on combinatorics, struggle with scalability for larger graphs. This paper introduces an automated framework for generating, augmenting, and analyzing unicyclic graphs using machine learning to predict key indices like degree distance. The framework enhances training datasets by systematically generating configurations and introducing structural diversity through edge perturbation and node reattachment. Evaluating models such as XGBoost and Support Vector Regression, we show that predictions closely match exact values, particularly for larger, unseen graphs. This approach improves scalability and accuracy, advancing graph analysis and network science.

articleTitle: Unstructuring the sequentiality of commits intoa semantic network with higher informational and functional quality
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Version control is an essential tool in software development, offering numerous well-known advantages, such as maintenance, traceability, collaborative work support, backup, and security. Commits provide the conceptual foundation of version control and contain helpful information for various stakeholders in the development and maintenance of applications, such as date, author, and a brief description of the changes made. Essentially, commits form a chronological sequence of data, but their utility is often underutilized and lacks efficiency in terms of accessibility. This paper presents an architectural solution that enables much greater utilization of commit history, providing more functional perspectives for accessing this rich source of knowledge-which often conveys experience, practical solutions, the rationale behind those solutions, and even reasons for discarding alternative options. The proposed architecture enhances developers' comprehension of intricate commit histories by enabling them to examine local changes and extract significant keywords from commit messages and code snippets. Because commit data is presented in a chronological sequence, it can be challenging to track dependencies and contextualize changes (commits). Our method facilitates sophisticated querying and visualization by arranging commit history into a graph structure representing thematic relationships among commits. Components for extracting commit data, processing it via a large language model (ChatGPT) to identify relevant keywords, storing the outcomes in a graph database, and applying different algorithmic solutions to “redesign” the dependencies between commits are all part of the architecture. The system enables effective keyword- based searching within the integrated development environment by clustering related commits based on shared keywords through community detection algorithms. To better assist developers in managing intricate codebases and enhancing teamwork.

articleTitle: Guarding the Gateways: CBP Cybersecurity Challenges and Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: With threats growing larger and more sophisticated, safeguarding the integrity of Customs and Border Protection (CBP) infrastructure has already served as an important line in national security. A breach in CBP's systems could potentially have dire consequences, causing not only significant financial loss and damage to their reputation, but also sacrificing national security at its very core. This research offers a comprehensive overview of key elements of cyber security strategies that aim to protect CBP's digital assets from certain types of high-stakes threats. These include ransomware, phishing, and insider attacks. It stresses the value of robust cybersecurity policies, such as proactive employee training, raw intensive policy-making and strategic reintegration of state-of-the-art technologies. By analyzing the latest attacks, this study discusses the 2019 United States (US) CBP data breach and analyses key areas for enhanced scrutiny. It calls for a proactive approach to cyber defense, one that prioritizes resilience and anticipates future threats to national security.

articleTitle: Integrating Snake Optimizer and SVR for Motor Rotor Temperature Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Motor rotor temperature is a critical parameter for ensuring reliable and safe operation of electric motors. Accurate temperature forecasting can help prevent thermal failures and provide valuable data for maintenance personnel. In this paper, a novel regression model that integrates Snake Optimizer (SO) with Support Vector Regression (SVR) is proposed to forecast the temperature of motor rotors. he principles of SO and SVR are introduced. The steps using SO to optimize the hyperparameters of SVR and the design process of fitness function are discussed in detail. Then, the hybrid model, SO-SVR, is established, which leads to improved prediction accuracy and robustness. To quantitatively evaluate the performance, experiments on public real-world data from a permanent magnet synchronous motor are conduct. The model is compared with other popular existing models, including MPA-ELM, WOA-RBF, and SSA-Elman, using Mean Absolute Error, Root Mean Square Error, and R-Squared. Results show that SO-SVR outperforms other models, achieving lower errors and higher robust. By accurately predicting motor rotor temperature, the developed model can reduce the occurrence of thermal failures and improve the reliability and safety of motor operation. The temperature data provided by the model also assists maintenance personnel in detecting and resolving potential issues before they become major problems.

articleTitle: Smart Training: Unleashing Your Potential with a Personal Intelligent Trainer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Maintaining a consistent fitness routine can be difficult for many individuals due to challenges such as lack of motivation, inadequate personalized guidance, and limited access to professional trainers. This research presents the Personal AI Trainer, an innovative, AI-powered virtual assistant designed to address these issues by offering personalized workout routines, real-time feedback, and continuous motivation based on the user's individual fitness data. The system utilizes advanced machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest for predicting health levels and XGBoost for estimating calorie expenditure and maximum weight lift potential. In addition, computer vision techniques are employed to count exercise repetitions and provide form feedback, creating an experience that closely mimics the interaction with a human trainer. The Personal AI Trainer is built to be adaptive and interactive, delivering customized fitness programs that evolve with the user's progress. Empirical studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the system in increasing user engagement, improving fitness outcomes, and sustaining long-term exercise habits. This solution provides a scalable, accessible, and cost-effective alternative to traditional personal trainers, making personalized fitness training more widely available to a broader audience.

articleTitle: Evaluating 3- D Features for Model Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper evaluates the performance of various al-gorithms in leveraging 3-D features for model matching. However, the lack of a common evaluation framework makes it challenging to compare different choices in the processing pipeline. In this paper, I introduce Proctor, an open-source framework designed for comparing 3-D features in model matching tasks. Proctor aims to foster easier sharing of ideas and methods by providing a modular architecture for evaluating various 3-D features. In-spired by successful standardization efforts in robotics and com-puter vision, Proctor offers a common platform for researchers to assess the performance of 3-D perception algorithms. I present the motivations behind Proctor and describe its modular archi-tecture, encouraging a community of users and contributors. The framework facilitates the comparison of different 3-D features, supporting tasks such as object recognition, pose estimation, and detection in clean or cluttered scenes. my evaluation includes a diverse range of features and datasets, demonstrating the effectiveness of Proctor in assessing the accuracy and speed of 3- D perception algorithms. Through Proctor, I aim to accelerate progress in 3-D perception research by providing a standardized platform for evaluating and comparing diverse approaches.

articleTitle: Viability Study Based on Saturation Resource in Data Centers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The evolution of Cloud Computing and the management of growing volumes of data require stable, high-performance and autonomous Data Centers. To guarantee the quality of optimal services, optimization and performance evaluation are essential to meet users' needs. This research highlights the importance of adapting infrastructures to ensure their long-term efficiency and sustainability. In particular, it examines the performance of the Elasticsearch engine during indexing and query processing, with the aim of preventing resource saturation. This paper presents the results of this viability study, focusing on the analysis of resource saturation.

articleTitle: Tackling Challenges in Life Sciences Master Data Management Through Effective Machine Learning Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Life sciences companies have always had to overcome specific master data management (MDM) challenges because of the massive, diverse and intricate clinical research records or patient data and regulatory mandates. It is critical that this data be well-managed to maintain efficient operations, meet various regulatory requirements and develop better patient outcomes. The transformative capabilities of machine learning (ML) can be great to simplify and streamline data integrations, improve data quality, as well as deliver predictive insights within MDM frameworks. While ML is not a silver bullet for life sciences MDM solutions thanks to data privacy issues, lack of standardization and scalability limitation where this may not make an impact. This paper also focuses on the barriers and provides recommendations for applying ML technologies in a practical approach within life sciences MDM. This study examines strategies for improving data management in life sciences, such as leveraging more advanced ML techniques like natural language processing (NLP) to work with unstructured data; anomaly detection to clean noisy or missingness in raw records and federated learning to train algorithms using privacy-preserving collaboration. This study uses a case studies and technical analysis approach to identify finally best practices and future research directions for utilizing the ML's full potential in life sciences MDM.

articleTitle: Maturity Model for Corporate Sector Based on Zero Trust Adoption
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The rapid evolution of cybersecurity threats necessitates the adoption of robust security frameworks. One such approach gaining significant attention is the concept of zero trust, which emphasizes continuous and strong verification, strict access controls and identity management, and well-planned strategy and assessment to mitigate risks. However, organizations often face challenges in effectively implementing and assessing their progress in zero trust adoption. We propose a maturity model for zero trust adoption, designed to assist organizations in evaluating their current security posture, identifying gaps, and developing a roadmap for achieving higher levels of zero trust maturity. The model encompasses various dimensions, including network segmentation, access controls, data protection, and incident response. Additionally, a comprehensive set of self-assessment queries is provided to enable organizations to gauge their progress and identify areas for improvement. Through the utilization of this maturity model and self-assessment framework, organizations can enhance their understanding of zero trust principles, align their security strategies, and prioritize necessary investments to strengthen their overall security posture.

articleTitle: Forecasting Future Tourism Demand to Popular Tourist Attractions to Asses Overtourism: A Machine Learning Modeling Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The research was aimed at estimating tourism demand in the medium term to Sri Lanka and the impact of potential high level of tourist arrivals resulting in overtourism and impacting sustainability in tourism to the most popular tourist attractions in Sri Lanka, namely Yala and Sigiriya. Yala is a nature preserve and a popular sight for sighting wild elephants and leopards using safari jeeps. Sigiriya is an ancient rock fortress considered a UNESCO world heritage that is climbed by foot. The two destinations are generally considered ‘must visit’ tourist attractions in a visit to Sri Lanka and could be subject to significant ‘tourist traffic’, particularly during the peak tourist months. Using a machine learning modeling approach, the study forecasts almost doubling of tourist arrivals to Sri Lanka from 2024 to 2027, in a mere 3 years. Based on the future demand, the study then estimated the future visitor demand as a count of daily safari jeeps to Yala and as a count of daily foot traffic to Sigiriya up to 2027, taking into consideration seasonality. The study suggests that the carrying capacity of both these tourist destinations to be significantly strained in the medium term. This is likely to adversely impact these environmentally and archeologically sensitive sites due to overtourism, particularly in peak tourist months, unless appropriate policy measures are taken to limit daily visitations to these sites.

articleTitle: Enhancing Threat Detection and Response Through Cloud-Native Security Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: In a dynamic cyber environment, the automation of threat detection and response has become critical in safeguarding sensitive information. The complexity and scale of traditional security systems make them inadequate to handle the modern cyber threats. Cloud-native security solutions, integrated into machine learning and artificial intelligence, provide an effective, scalable, and automated way to detect and mitigate security threats in real time. Such solutions exploit the natively scalable, flexible, and resilient nature of cloud infrastructures. This paper deliberates on the contribution of cloud-native security tools towards the automation of threat detection and response. Based on architecture, functionality, and effectiveness of such solutions, we analyze their case studies emanating from top-notched cloud providers. In such case studies, we explained how real-time data analysis is leveraged to automatically discover potential threats like zero-day attacks and insider threats. Our study also includes performance results based on cloud-native architectures, presented in the way they minimize human intervention and speed up responses. Automating the process made it possible for businesses to pay more attention to proactive security measures and thereby mitigate possible breaches with more ease. In conclusion, a cloud-native security automation transforms the entire way that enterprises protect their assets against threats. It provides a risk-proofed solution for the future, reassuring people of safety from new and emerging risks.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Driven Detection of Malicious URLs and Network Intrusions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The detection of malicious URLs and network intrusions is a critical task in cybersecurity. This study investigates the application of several machine learning models to classify network traffic data for intrusion detection purposes. The dataset, obtained, comprises 4,998 instances with 32 features related to network traffic attributes. Data preprocessing steps including normalization and feature selection based on information gain were applied. The study evaluates the performance of various classification algorithms, such as Support Vector Machines (SVM), AdaBoost, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Gaussian Naive Bayes. The XGBoost classifier achieves the highest accuracy of 92.1 %, demonstrating its effectiveness in detecting intrusions across several intrusion classes. The results highlight the potential of machine learning techniques in enhancing cybersecurity through malicious URLs and intrusion detection.

articleTitle: BiPath-CNet: Optimizing R-Peak Detection Leveraging Bi-Pathway Cardio Network with Spectral Temporal Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: R-peak detection is critical for accurate cardiac signal analysis, and traditional models often struggle with varying signal complexities. This study proposes a Bi-pathway cardio network (BiPath-CNet), an innovative deep learning (DL) model augmented with a Spectral Temporal Attention Mechanism (STAM) to enhance R-peak detection in electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. The proposed BiPath-CNet leverages STAM to dynamically capture spectral and temporal dependencies in ECG data, ensuring more precise feature extraction and robust peak detection. Extensive experiments demonstrate that BiPath-CNet performed better than several conventional DL models offering significant improvements in detection accuracy, recall, and precision. Integrating frequency-aware routing and temporal gating in STAM empowers the model to highlight critical signal components minimizing detection errors. This architecture offers a promising advancement in ECG signal analysis, enhancing the application of DL practices in biomedical research.

articleTitle: Bioelectronic Monitoring of Monocyte-to-Macrophage Differentiation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Monocytes, a major player in the immune system responses, differentiate into macrophages under the influence of various environmental factors. Understanding the complex differentiation mechanism is crucial for the development and discovery of targeted therapies. However, conventional methods used are mainly end-point assays, often time-consuming and labor-intensive. Real-time and higher throughput monitoring of the differentiation process can enable dynamic testing of this process hence increasing the biological relevance. We have developed a microfabricated bioelectronic platform aiming to monitor M0 macrophage transition from suspension to adherent cells, indicative of their successful differentiation. Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS), is used as the active electrode due to its considerably lower impedance compared to conventional metal electrodes rendering it more sensitive to monitor cells attachment on the electrode. PEDOT:PSS is patterned into a microfabricated gold electrode array while well-designed PDMS-based wells are placed atop to confine the cells on the PEDOT:PSS-coated electrode array. The differentiation of suspension THP-l monocytes to adherent M0 macrophages is monitored by measuring the changes in the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy spectra of the electrode at the different stages of cell transition. The device demonstrates sensitivity in detecting cell adhesion (hence THP-l differentiation) on the PEDOT:PSS electrode surfaces, where PEDOT:PSS provides a suitable environment for cell growth and differentiation while being electrically conducting for signal transduction. The developed bioelectronic platform, combining conducting polymer electrode arrays for sensitivity and microwells for cell confinement and higher throughput can be further used for various cell-based assays given its versatility and ease in fabrication and operation.

articleTitle: Social Computing Interactions and Fusion AI Development for Teaching and Entertainment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Integrating social computing with a combination of AI improvement offers transformative potential for both instructing and exciting applications. This paper investigates how social computing-characterized by collaborative and intelligent client behavior in advanced environments-can be improved through AI advances to make more personalized, engaging, and versatile encounters. Within the instruction set, AI-driven social computing frameworks empower clever coaching, real-time input, and peer collaboration, cultivating higher levels of understudy engagement and personalized learning pathways. In amusement, AI-powered social stages can create immersive, intelligently encounters custom-fitted to person inclinations, advertising unused shapes of substance creation and client support. Be that as it may, whereas these innovations hold excellent guarantees, they, too, show critical challenges, such as guaranteeing client security, tending to moral concerns, and planning frameworks that viably adjust human and machine intelligence. This paper analyzes the benefits, potential applications, and challenges of blending social computing with AI within instruction and excitement, giving a system for future inquiry about and advancement in this advancing space.

articleTitle: Emotion Analysis Using Multimodal Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: As part of the various treatments and explorations of massive data on the web, emotion modelling is part of a method that aims to understand and predict users' emotional states. Behavioral analysis from multimedia content enables the detection of reactions and attitudes elicited by the music and lyrics of a song. This paper presents the development of a Deep Learning-based model for analyzing listeners' emotions from multimodal data, which also aims to optimize decision-making based on these reactions. Efficient classification of emotions will contribute to the optimization of recommendation systems.

articleTitle: Optimized Energy Management in Solar-Powered Parking Lot with Integrating Green Hydrogen Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper presents an optimized energy management system for a solar-powered parking lot integrated with green hydrogen storage. The proposed system uses photovoltaic (PV) panels to generate electricity, which is either used for charging electric vehicles (EVs) or converted into hydrogen for storage via a water electrolyzer. The stored hydrogen not only powers fuel cells to generate electricity during periods of low solar output, but also directly supplies hydrogen vehicles (HVs), ensuring continuous energy availability for both EVs and HVs. The energy management model aims to minimize operational costs and enhance system reliability by efficiently distributing solar energy between EV charging, hydrogen production, and hydrogen supply for HVs. The optimization process is conducted using the Crested Porcupine Optimizer (CPO) algorithm, which ensures the system's robust performance under varying solar conditions and energy demands. Simulation results demonstrate that integrating green hydrogen storage significantly improves energy efficiency, reduces reliance on the grid, and lowers overall operating costs by 1.6%.

articleTitle: Optimal sizing of on-grid solar-battery system considering cost, reliability and emission
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This study focuses on the optimal sizing on solar PV hybrid systems, taking into account the cost implications, reliability and emissions. Renewable energy sources, particularly solar PV is beginning to have reduced operational costs and environmental benefits, making it a desirable sustainable energy solution. However, combining the assessment of cost, reliability and environmental impact makes the sizing process challenging, turning it into a multi criteria decision making problem. This paper uses a metaheuristic optimization method called Leaders and Followers (LaF) algorithm to determine the best economical, reliable and low emission configuration for an on-grid solar PV hybrid system. The findings demonstrate that larger PV and battery systems minimize grid dependence and emissions while increasing dependability, providing practical advice for optimal solar PV hybrid design in commercial and industrial applications.

articleTitle: Multimodal Paper Summarization with Hierarchical Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Modern scientific articles extend beyond plain text, with publishers such as Elsevier frequently supplementing their papers with videos and graphical abstracts (infographic summaries) to enhance the reading experience. Currently, paper summarizers capable of effectively fusing two or more modalities are scarce, and the complexity of integrating these diverse modalities, often with missing or incomplete data, calls for advanced modelling technologies. This paper introduces Hier-SciSum, a new model for Multimodal Paper Summarization (MPS), Hier-SciSum incorporates a Hierarchical Multimodal Fusion (HMF) module, which effectively integrates diverse modalities by first capturing pairwise intrinsic cross-modality correlations through attention mechanisms and then refining these relationships with cross-attention masking. This hierarchical approach allows for a progressive understanding of both low-level pairwise relationships and higher-level integrated representations. Extensive experiments conducted on a newly introduced MPS dataset showcase our model's effectiveness. Impressively, Hier-SciSum generates high-quality summaries, outperforming both uni- and multi-modality models.

articleTitle: ES-ATF: Early Smoke Detection based on Attention-aggregated Temporal Feature Extraction*
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Smoke detection is an area where strong research interest was put since its practical meaning in extinguishing fire in the early stage. Detecting smoke not only reduces the life or property loss but also has environment-protection value as inefficient combustion can be restricted. In the literature, there are bunches of investigations on single-frame smoke detection via YOLO-based methods, however, these methods are always attenuated by the transparency and imperceptibility nature of smoke. Therefore, more useful information that can work as an extra prompt to the model is expected. To strengthen the information density of inputs, one possible solution is to explore inter-frame correlation within a smoke snippet. With this added temporal information, a boost in model performance can be expected. This paper adopts an attention-aggregated temporal feature extraction method, by which, the inter-image feature can be better exploited, and more frames can be detected at one time. Consequently, the smoke detection process is speeding up while simultaneously, the model's capability is enhanced in terms of alarming a potential smoke before it evolves to the late stage.

articleTitle: Robustness of the Compositional Data Approach in Bipolar Psychometric Likert Scales Big Bimodal Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Managerial decision making, the enhancement of recommender systems, the prediction of human behaviour and the selection of adequate psychotherapeutic measures all depend on individual attitudes, preferences and psychometric profiles. To gather these, bipolar psychometric questionnaires are used among other methods. Recently, the compositional data structure known as the Simplex was identified in bipolar Likert scale data. This concept posits that any level of agreement with an item assertion implies a level of disagreement, resulting in bivariate compositional information. Applying standard statistical procedure (e.g., computation of mean, standard deviation, linear regression etc.) to Simplex data yields biased results. Through the use of an isometric log-ratio (ilr) transformation, bivariate data can be converted to a real-valued interval scale where means and sums of item responses remain unbiased. Correlations form the basis of many psychometric big data analyses including, but not limited to, linear regression models (including structural equation models, partial least squares path modeling and moderator analysis), development and validation of bipolar Likert scales and econometric decision making. It is well-established that the ilr approach enhances the statistical power of correlation tests based on Student's t-distribution, provided that the Central Limit Theorem (CLT) holds true. However, in practical applications, adherence to the CLT depends on factors such as the number of items and the distribution shape of the data generating process (DGP). Psychometric data may consist of only a few item responses, and DGPs can exhibit bimodality, leading to violations of the CLT. Through simulation studies, we demonstrate that the ilr approach performs effectively even when the CLT assumptions regarding bimodality and small item numbers are violated, thereby increasing the statistical power of correlation tests. This research extends previous findings.

articleTitle: Posture Monitoring and Classification for Health Care of Bedridden Patients Using IoT and AI Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Posture monitoring has become a crucial area of research and application, particularly considering the increasing concerns about musculoskeletal disorders and their association with prolonged lying and poor ergonomic practices. To solve the crucial problem of bedridden patient care, this study investigates the categorization of lying postures using four different deep learning models: The models used are Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), VGG16, and ResNe<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex>50. Due to bedridden patients' difficulty in developing pressure ulcers, respiratory disorders, and other complications, the classification of laying positions which includes supine, prone, and lateral is essential. Some possible assistive devices that can inform caregivers or initiate some techniques to improve the patient's comfort and eliminate adverse effects of immobility can benefit from the identification of some postures in real-time. The models were trained using both balanced and unbalanced data sets from a set of labeled images covering different laying postures. Their performance was then determined by criteria including accuracy, RMSE, Kappa, recall, and precision. As for the performance, the proposed VGG model achieved better classification accuracy compared to the CNN, RNN, and ResNet models. In light of enhancing patient care as well as monitoring within the health care facilities, it is suggested from our result that these models could suggest potential solutions to posture identification for bedridden patients. By illustrating how AI posture classification systems can be implemented in IoT-based applications, the study also shows how future healthcare delivery can be improved and the problems caused by long periods of inactivity can be prevented.

articleTitle: Audcare: Advanced Care for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder Through a Mobile Application for Predicting and Managing Meltdowns Using CNN-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) often experience unpredictable meltdowns due to complex behavioral and environmental factors. A lack of accessible information on prevention and management strategies, along with a shortage of specialized healthcare professionals, complicates support for families.
