This study develops a mobile application that predicts meltdowns, featuring a recommendation engine for prevention strategies and a location-based service for nearby healthcare providers. The app utilizes the CNN-LSTM model (MoViNets) to classify tantrums and generate tailored strategies. The MoViNets model achieved training and validation accuracies of 82.03 % and 87.30%, respectively, with an overall classification accuracy of 90%. Evaluations from therapy centers indicated strong functionality (mean of 4.33), usability (4.19), reliability (4.14), and security (4.40), resulting in an overall mean rating of 4.27, signifying a well-rounded system in terms of functionality and user experience.

Author Keywords: Mobile Video Networks for Efficient Video Recognition

articleTitle: Sahub - Stackoverflow and Comments Integrations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach for connecting StackOverflow discussions and open source codebases through a graph database model in Neo4j. By encouraging developers to adopt a structured annotation framework using widely known tags such as @ author, @description, @ link, @tags, and optional fields such as @operatingSystem and @fileExtension, the paper will discuss how to link code snippets to specific technical questions. These annotations are then analyzed, creating an interconnected knowledge graph that can associate StackOver-flow questions with real-world code examples and additional documentation pulled directly from code snippets.

articleTitle: Securing Local E-Commerce Businesses Against Cyber Attacks Using Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Local e-commerce businesses face critical cybersecurity threats such as fake reviews, phishing attacks, and brute-force logins. This paper introduces RealCheck, a deep learning-driven cybersecurity framework integrating NLP, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and CAPTCHA systems to detect fraudulent reviews, block malicious URLs, and prevent unauthorized access. Evaluated against ISO 25010:2011 standards, RealCheck achieved high accuracy and reliability, demonstrating its potential to safeguard small-scale e-commerce platforms. By addressing these challenges through an AI-driven, multi-layered approach, this work offers a practical and scalable solution tailored to local e-commerce needs.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Feature Selection Techniques for Eye Movement Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Electrooculography (EOG) has been widely applied across a range of applications, such as medical diagnosis, assistive technology, and human computer interface interactions. The current study examines the classification of four eye movements (right, left, up, and down) through electrooculography (EOG) signals, testing two feature selection methods: adaptive analysis of variances (ANOVA) and forward feature selection. The objective of this study is to select the most relevant features, among the used statistical, while maintaining a high accuracy level for identifying eye movements. Applying the adaptive ANOVA feature selection method, a maximum classification accuracy of 95.6% was achieved, while the forward feature selection method demonstrated higher performance with an accuracy of 98.7%. The highest accuracy was reached by performing several classification methods in each trial, including K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Decision Trees (DT). The results indicate the impact of feature selection in enhancing classifier performance.

articleTitle: Lightweight Cryptography for IoT Platforms: Enhancing Security in Embedded Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: An unprecedented demand for robust security solutions designed to operate within embedded systems constraints has arisen due to the enormous expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) devices. This research paper investigates the importance of lightweight cryptography (LWC) for solving these challenges, particularly with regard to implementation on resource constrained IoT platforms and embedded devices. We investigate current security challenges, survey lightweight cryptographic solutions, and explore implementation approaches on hardware and software platforms.

articleTitle: Decoding Contralateral Finger Movements from fNIRS Signals Using Phase Connectivity Features
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), an emerging and non-invasive neuroimaging tool, holds great promise for brain-computer interface (BCI) applications and diagnostics due to its portability, ease of use, and ability to monitor cerebral hemodynamics. BCIs traditionally rely on amplitude-based features for decoding motor activities, but the potential of phase connectivity features has been rarely explored. This study explores the feasibility of decoding contralateral finger movements using fNIRS signals with phase connectivity features. fNIRS data from five subjects performing motor tasks involving left- and right-hand finger tapping, along with a control condition, were analyzed. Preprocessing steps included noise reduction, conversion to oxyhemoglobin and deoxyhemoglobin concentrations, and extraction of statistical features and phase-based connectivity metrics, including phase-locking value (PLV) and magnitude-squared coherence (MSC), were employed. The classification of tapping conditions was conducted using various machine learning algorithms, including support vector machines (SVM), random forests (RF), k-nearest neighbors (k-NN), and artificial neural networks (ANNs). Our results demonstrate that combining statistical and phase-based connectivity features significantly enhances classification accuracy, with k-NN achieving the highest average performance of 96.1 ± 0.18%. These findings highlight the potential of fNIRS with phase connectivity features to decode fine motor movements, offering novel insights into neuroprosthetic applications and BCIs.

articleTitle: Integrating AI and Semi-Immersive AR Technology for Brain Tumor Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Brain tumours, characterised by abnormal cell development inside the brain, pose a significant risk to individuals due to their high mortality rate. Early identification is essential for accurate diagnosis and successful treatment to enhance patient outcomes. However, diagnosing small tumours can be difficult and error-prone, as it largely depends on the experience and qualifications of medical personnel. Therefore, an automated diagnostic approach that reduces diagnostic time while increasing accuracy is desperately needed. This study addresses the challenges of manual diagnosis by applying deep learning algorithms to brain tumour segmentation. Additional challenges in applying deep learning for tumour segmentation include handling low-quality scans, variations in tumour features, and insufficient data. We present an emerging concept combining Artificial Intelligence and Augmented Reality as a valuable tool, providing deep learning model deployment, immersive visualisation, and interactive functionalities to support diagnosis and surgical interventions for brain tumours. The achieved performance is competitive with the literature, and feedback from medical professionals after deployment evaluation is satisfactory.

articleTitle: Smart IoT-Based Solution for Emergency Assistance during Sandstorms and Landslides
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Natural disasters, which are caused by changes in the climate and geography, pose a major threat to human life and economic stability. These events, which include cyclones, tsunamis, landslides, and earthquakes, can result in serious ecological damage as well as fatalities. The speed at which climate change is occurring increases the unpredictability of such disasters, especially in vulnerable regions like deserts and forests. This study offers a solution to the challenges of rescuing those who are stranded by such catastrophes, where traditional rescue methods and communication may not be effective. The system uses Internet of Things (IoT) and mobile phone technologies to send location information and real-time alerts through Global Positioning System (GPS) and Geographic Information System (GIS), enabling the timely location of a person or vehicle for effective emergency response. This approach aims to improve disaster preparedness and survival rates in remote, catastrophe-prone areas.

articleTitle: Evaluation of GHI from NASA MERRA-2 and ECMWF ERA5-Land Reanalysis Against In-Situ Observations in Al-Ain, UAE
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Solar reanalysis datasets are a valuable resource for estimating solar energy potential in situations where in-situ solar measurements are not available. A detailed assessment with short-term in-situ data is crucial to evaluate and understand the extent of errors. This study evaluates Global Horizontal Irradiance (GHI) reanalysis data from NASA's MERRA-2 and ECMWF's ERA5-Land, using high-quality in-situ observations collected in Al-Ain, UAE. The evaluation spans from January 1 to December 31, 2022, and employs statistical metrics such as Relative Mean Bias Error (rMBE), Relative Mean Absolute Error (rMAE), Relative Root Mean Square Error (rRMSE), and the Coefficient of Determination (R2). The analysis reveals that for Al-Ain, the annual ranges for rMBE, rRMSE, and R2 are 2.9-6.2%, 5.0-8.1%, and 0.941-0.980 for ERA5-Land, and 8.7-13.6%, 12.6-15.9%, and 0.919-0.959 for MERRA-2. Findings indicate that MERRA-2 and ERA5-Land yield comparable accuracy under clear sky conditions, whereas ERA5-Land consistently outperformed MERRA-2 across all error metrics for both all-sky and clear-sky conditions, demonstrating lower bias and greater accuracy..

articleTitle: A Novel Two-Step Hybrid Quantum Watermarking Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The paper presents a novel hybrid quantum water-marking method designed to enhance the security and robustness of digital media protection. The proposed scheme integrates a two-step encryption process, achieving high security while pre-serving quality. Key features include classical LSB substitution, quantum chaos matrix, and an improved quantum representation, offering superior resistance to attacks. By combining spatial and transform domain encryption, the method overcomes vulner-abilities in singular value decomposition, enhancing robustness and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR). Compared to the latest developments-such as sinusoidal-tent map, multi-scale pattern-based quantum text watermarking (MPQTW), maximum pixel difference, tri-way pixel, and NEQR with Quantum Majority Finder (QMF)-the proposed approach shows an average PSNR improvement of approximately 20 % and a significant reduction in Bit Error Rate (BER) by 15.41 %. Additionally, the method demonstrates strong resistance to various attack types with a correlation two-dimensional (Corr 2D) value near 1, such as 0.994 against salt and pepper noise attacks. These results highlight a significant advancement in quantum watermarking technology, balancing improved perceptual quality, security, and robustness.

articleTitle: Decoding Diabetes: Unconventional Indicators for Diabetic Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Diabetes diagnosis has always involved glucose tests; however, it is possible to recognize diabetic complications by simply looking at skin and nails. This work presents a new approach for identifying diabetes-related complications, including acanthosis nigricans, foot ulcers, and nail infections, utilizing and TensorFlow for deep learning. Both conditions are associated with visual signals and pass through a strictly trained dataset, marked up for maximum accuracy. From the methodologies, including image resizing, data augmentation, and hyperparameter tuning. The findings of accuracy confirm that the platform should register specific characteristics of the problem area and has the essential precision to maintain close attention to possible risks of diabetes and intervene early to reduce the likelihood of patients' deteriorating health.

articleTitle: Impact of Window Glazing and Lighting Controls on Energy Performance Analysis of Public Buildings: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This study comprehensively evaluates the energy performance of a public building at Viale Piceno, 60 (Citta Metropolitana di Milano), Milan, Italy, using the EnergyPlus-based Design Builder simulation platform. The analysis focuses on the impact of advanced glazing technologies and lighting controls on energy efficiency. A baseline configuration with triple-glazed low-emissivity windows recorded an annual energy consumption of 527,491.9 kWh., serving as the benchmark for comparative analysis. This study evaluates various upgrade scenarios to assess their influence on heating, cooling, and overall energy performance, including SageGlass (available in double- and triple-glazed formats), thermochromic glazing, and lighting control. SageGlass ClimaPlus Green glazing and lighting controls demonstrated the highest efficiency gains, reducing total energy consumption by up to 37.3%, primarily through substantial cooling demand reductions. This research highlights the potential of advanced technologies to enhance energy efficiency, lower costs, and promote sustainable public infrastructure.

articleTitle: Knowledge Graphs and Machine Learning in Fake News and Disinformation Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The rise of digital platforms has facilitated the rapid spread of disinformation, which poses significant social, political, and economic challenges. Knowledge graphs (KGs) are emerging as effective tools for enhancing the accuracy, interpretability, and scalability of fake news detection systems, addressing limitations in traditional machine learning-based approaches that rely pri-marily on linguistic analysis. This work contains a literature review that synthesizes findings from recent studies on the application of KGs in disinformation detection. We identify how KGs improve detection by encoding real relationships, analyzing context, and enhancing model interpretability, while also discussing current limitations in scalability, data completeness, and contextual adaptability. The reviewed studies underscore the need for future research focusing on scalable, real-time, and cross-linguistic KG models to bolster disinformation detection capabilities globally. Moreover, we present preliminary results of two use cases, showcasing a methodology for constructing KGs that can serve as useful tools to fight against disinformation spread.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Applications for Wind Energy Forecasting in Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Driven by the pressing need for sustainable and reliable energy sources, this paper critically evaluates deep learning's role in advancing wind energy forecasting, highlighting its potential to address current energy demands through improved prediction accuracy. Due to the inherent unpredictability of wind, conventional forecasting models often fall short; however, deep learning models offer enhanced reliability by effectively identifying complex, embedded patterns within wind data. The paper examines techniques such as time-series recurrent neural networks, restricted Boltzmann machines, convolutional neural networks, and autoencoders, each targeting distinct challenges in wind forecasting to strengthen grid integration and ensure energy reliability. Future directions-including hybrid model approaches and model interpretability-are discussed, underscoring deep learning's promise as a powerful tool for optimizing wind energy utilization and supporting a more sustainable, low-carbon energy infrastructure.

articleTitle: Transforming the Future: An Innovative LiFi Framework to Elevate Sustainability and Security in UAE Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The rapid advancement of smart cities calls for the implementation of cutting-edge communication solutions that are capable of effectively addressing the myriad challenges associated with sustainability and security. This comprehensive research presents the innovative concept of integrating Light-Fidelity (LiFi) technology as a pivotal element for significantly enhancing smart city infrastructures, with a strong emphasis on its application in the United Arab Emirates. By harnessing the exceptional capabilities of light-emitting diodes (LEDs), LiFi offers a significantly low-energy, high-speed alternative to traditional Wi- Fi systems by utilizing visible light as the medium for the transmission of data. This in-depth investigation delves into the various ways through which LiFi enhances security measures by restricting communication to designated areas that are illuminated while simultaneously minimizing overall energy consumption, thus strongly supporting the sustainable development goals aimed at fostering smart cities. The thorough framework assesses the practicality, economic viability, and comprehensive security measures associated with the potential implementation of LiFi in diverse urban settings. Additionally, it proposes a sustainable communication method that effectively combats escalating energy demands, strategically targets areas lacking adequate Wi-Fi coverage, and addresses the prevalent security concerns that are common in densely populated city environments. The detailed results emphasize LiFi's transformative potential to revolutionize urban communication networks, aligning seamlessly with the ambitious aspirations of the UAE towards innovative and sustainable smart city initiatives.

articleTitle: Enhancing Behavioral Analytics with Zero Trust in Cloud: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The digital age of technology has paved the way for advanced methods like cloud computing that have completely revolutionized the way traditional systems in organizations work. This advancement in cloud computing provides an effective way to handle large amounts of data, applications, and services. As with any critical system, the security of the cloud is of utmost importance. Researchers used the zero trust model working on the principle “never trust, always verify” to provide security to cloud computing. This model continuously verifies and monitors the interactions of users and devices to provide a robust security framework. Behavioral analytics, which has become important due to its ability to detect anomalies, has been integrated with the zero-trust model to enhance detection and provide efficient security measures against threats. However, a variety of limitations still needs to be addressed to further enhance behavioral analytics with zero trust. To address this, in this paper, we performed a study of zero trust model architecture and its steps of implementation. We also explored different zero trust mechanisms and their integration with behavioral analytics. We also evaluated the existing work by drawing a comparison between them based on their strengths and weaknesses. We identified the gaps present in the existing mechanisms and then based on that we gave future directions that will be beneficial for future researchers. Overall, our work provides an effective insight into existing problems and provides a direction for future progress for the researchers.

articleTitle: Ensemble Machine Learning-Based Intrusion Detection System for Securing the Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: With the rapid growth of smart devices, IoT networks have become an essential part of our daily lives, but they're also increasingly vulnerable to cyberattacks. Traditional intrusion detection systems (IDSs) often struggle to keep up with the growing complexity of these threats, leading to delays in detection and a high rate of false alarms. To tackle this, we developed an Ensemble Intrusion Detection System (EIDS) that combines the strengths of several machine learning algorithms through a Stacking Classifier. At its core, our system uses Logistic Regression as a meta-learner and integrates Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), and Gradient Boosting (GB) classifiers. By addressing data imbalance with the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) on the NSL-KDD dataset, we ensured fair and effective training. Our approach achieves an impressive 97.62% accuracy, making it not only more reliable but also better at minimizing false positives. This solution brings us one step closer to securing IoT networks against the evolving landscape of cyber threats.

articleTitle: A Review of Machine Learning Methods for Screening Cardiac Abnormalities using Auscultation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper presents a thorough review of various methodologies employed in heart sound classification, combining both conventional machine learning (ML) algorithms and complex deep learning (DL) approaches. We systematically evaluate different data collection approaches, preprocessing techniques, methodologies, and classification mechanisms. Further-more, the review analyzes several feature extraction methods required for capturing relevant signal characteristics, spanning Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC), continuous wavelet transform (CWT), and convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Additionally, we examine a variety of classification methods, from traditional methods like support vector machines (SVMs), Knearest neighbors (KNNs), and Decision Trees (DTs), to more sophisticated parametric approaches such as recurrent neural networks (RNNs), (CNNs), long-short term memory (LSTM), and even ensemble techniques, signifying the potential of combining classification approaches. Key findings reveal a trend toward employing hybrid models that merge the capabilities of multiple techniques to enhance cardiac diagnostics precision. This comprehensive overview aims to explore existing methodologies and move toward bridging the gap in today's technologies, establishing a robust diagnostic tool for medical applications.

articleTitle: Coordination Strategies for Vacating a Parking Lot
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This study explores the coordination issues that may arise in the first-mile logistics of the automotive industry when a production plant requires the services of an independent transportation company to vacate a parking lot. The interaction between the previous agents as a simultaneous game where they have the same strategies, but opposite preferences is modeled. In such a case, it is shown that coordination issues happen because of multiple Nash equilibria; each equilibrium benefits one agent and harms the other. Since agents do not have incentives to deviate from their Nash equilibrium strategies, some mechanisms based on incentives, information sharing, and vendor management to induce a unique Nash equilibrium are discussed. So, such mechanisms contribute to facilitating coordination in the first-mile logistics of the automotive industry.

articleTitle: Evaluating Datagram Congestion Control Protocol (DCCP) for Real-Time Applications: A Comparative Study with TCP in Multi-Node Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The rise in demand for real-time applications, such as live streaming, online gaming, and Internet telephony, has highlighted the necessity for transport protocols that offer low latency and network stability. Traditional protocols, namely Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and User Datagram Protocol (UDP), have inherent limitations. TCP ensures reliable data delivery but suffers from latency, making it unsuitable for real-time needs, while UDP provides fast data transmission but lacks congestion control, which can lead to network instability. This gap underscores the need for a protocol that combines high-speed data transfer with effective congestion management. To address this issue, the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) introduced the Datagram Congestion Control Protocol (DCCP), designed to optimize data delivery speed while managing congestion. This study evaluates DCCP's performance against TCP in network scenarios of 8 and 16 nodes using the NS2 simulation environment. By comparing throughput and delay across various bandwidth and latency settings, the study finds that DCCP offers up to 35% higher throughput in 8-node setups and reduces packet loss by 20% in high-bandwidth scenarios. These results suggest that DCCP is well-suited for real-time applications, achieving a crucial balance between fast data transmission and network stability.

articleTitle: Optimized Deep Learning Framework for Arabic Handwritten Character Recognition Using Coati Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Automatic handwritten character recognition is one of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications considered a stimulating field of research and significant in different domains. Numerous studies have concentrated on detecting English handwritten characters, with several addressing Arabic handwriting due to the diverse shapes of characters based on their positions in words. Despite these efforts, there are still opportunities to improve Arabic handwritten letter recognition. Deep learning (DL) presents a promising approach, as it can effectively handle large volumes of unlabeled raw data, which is increasingly available today. Therefore, this article presents an Optimized Deep Learning Framework for Arabic Handwritten Character Recognition using the Coati Optimization Algorithm (ODLF-AHCRCOA) technique. The ODLF-AHCRCOA technique aims to recognize the distinct handwritten characters in Arabic. To accomplish this, the Sobel filter (SF) is utilized for image preprocessing to enhance edge detection. The modified LeN et-5 method is employed for feature extraction to capture high-dimensional representations of character features. Moreover, the long short-term memory (LSTM) classifier is used to classify Arabic handwritten characters. To improve the classification accuracy, the coati optimization algorithm (COA) is implemented for parameter tuning, optimizing the LSTM hyperparameters of the model for enhanced convergence and performance. The simulation study of the ODLF-AHCRCOA method is performed, and the outcomes are examined using varying features. The experimental validation of the ODLF-AHCRCOA method exhibited a superior accuracy value of 98.60% over other approaches.

articleTitle: Utilizing MRI Scans and Machine Learning to Enhance Depression Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Depressive disorder rates have been increasing rapidly in recent history, and our paper offers the groundwork for a tool to combat this rise. Many therapists rely largely on qualitative analysis when diagnosing depressive disorders, however, our aim is to provide a more quantitative analysis in classifying depression and its severity. Whereas most modern techniques for diagnosing depression are dependent upon surveys and questionnaires as well as interviews, our solution utilizes neuroimaging techniques, particularly, MRI scans. This paper demonstrates the usage of multiple machine learning methods acting on a set of MRI scans allowing the models to diagnose depression and give an indicator of its severity. Our MRI scans are obtained through a publicly available dataset on OpenNeuro. If our research is implemented in therapist and psychologists' offices, we can potentially increase the accuracy of the diagnoses that are made by professionals thereby improving the treatment that patients receive.

articleTitle: Advanced Modelling of Energy Losses in Railway Vehicles Considering Temperature Dependencies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper presents the modelling and simulation of energy losses in the drive train of railway vehicles, considering nonlinear loss characteristics, temperature dependencies, and operation point deviations due to individual load distributions. Multidimensional look-up tables (LUTs) are employed to accurately determine the component losses within the drivetrain of railway vehicles. Both Cauer and Foster thermal models are implemented to calculate the temperatures of the components. By comparing the resulting operating points of different axles, the influence of load distribution on component losses is analysed. The evaluation of multiple test cases highlights the significant impact of temperature dependencies on component losses. Different assumptions regarding component temperatures can result in variations in total losses by up to 14 percentage points when compared to the worst-case scenario. Consequently, ignoring temperature dependencies can lead to significantly erroneous outcomes.

articleTitle: Holistic Fitness Tracking by Integrating Environmental Data Monitoring With Health Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The problem with conventional fitness trackers is that they take their measurements in isolation from external environmental conditions. Several studies have disclosed that the effectiveness of physical exertion is not a function of only internal parameters like heart rate and step rate, but also largely dependent on external parameters such as air quality index and temperature. In fact, prolonged exposure to poor air quality during elevated metabolism periods (work-out periods) can affect the individual's cognition in addition to deteriorating their physical exertion capability. The reason why air quality monitors are not conventionally included in portable fitness trackers is because of their typical large sizes. In this paper, we explore a way to miniaturise these air quality monitors in order to integrate them into a portable system for outdoor exercising. The means is via a system comprising of two wearable devices in intermittent wireless communication. One of the devices is worn on the wrist for monitoring the athlete's internal vitals, while the other is worn on the arm for monitoring air quality parameters like particulate matter concentration and humidity. Data collected is uploaded to an online database at hourly intervals for evaluation by health professionals should the need arise. After testing, the device was found to give impressive step counting accuracies of between 90 and 98 percent, and convenient battery lives of 7 hours and 12 hours. The whole system recorded a combined weight of 450g, making it excellently portable and non-disruptive to athlete workouts.

articleTitle: Development of a Chatbot to Support an University Institutional Website
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Currently, the institutional website of the Polytechnic Institute of Bragança (IPB) lacks an interactive system that allows users to obtain information quickly and efficiently. With the increase in the use of online services and the preference of students for instant interactions, there is a growing need for tools that facilitate communication and access to information. This work proposes the development of a chatbot to support the IPB website, with the aim of improving user experience and providing quick and accurate answers to their queries. The main objective of this project is to create an intelligent chatbot capable of understanding and responding to a wide range of questions related to IPB. To achieve this, modern natural language processing and machine learning technologies such as Streamlit, Langchain, and OpenAI are used. The system includes an automated Web Scraper to keep information up-to-date, an architecture based on efficient document segmentation, and an administrative back office for monitoring and management. This development represents a significant advance in how users interact with the IPB website, offering a more efficient and accessible communication channel. The chatbot has the potential to reduce the workload of administrative staff while improving user satisfaction by providing accurate and instant answers to their questions.

articleTitle: Detecting Deepfakes in Healthcare: A Review and Proposed Solution
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The widespread use of Deepfake technology presents serious challenges to the integrity and security of healthcare systems. This study provides a detailed review of Deepfake de-tection methods designed particularly for the healthcare domain. We investigate the present methodologies, privacy concerns, and data security risks associated with Deepfakes in medical contexts. Based on a thorough analysis of the current literature, we offer a new approach framework for healthcare-specific Deepfake detection that incorporates powerful machine learning algorithms and privacy-preserving strategies. We highlight research gaps, challenges, and future possibilities for research in this crucial domain, emphasizing the need for reliable, ethical, and adaptive Deepfake detection systems in healthcare.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Enhanced Graph Neural Networks for Multi-Scale, Richly Labeled Networks in Interconnected Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The study of interconnected, multi-scale networks is essential in uncovering complex relationships across diverse domains, such as biomedical research, information security, and social sciences. This paper introduces a novel framework that integrates Reinforcement Learning (RL) with Graph Neural Net-works (GNNs) for analyzing multi-scale, richly labeled networks. Most traditional GNN architectures cannot effectively represent heterogeneous data that are in continuous evolution at multiple scales of interaction. Our framework overcomes these limitations by leveraging an RL agent to optimize multi-scale attention and label encoding with regard to real-time network dynamics, hence ensuring better adaptability and scalability of the model across domains like gene-protein interaction networks, tracking influence in social media, and detection of advanced persistent threats. The results underscore the efficacy of combining RL and GNNs for improved cross-domain analysis, contributing significantly to the field of complex network modeling.

articleTitle: Robust and Reliable Assessment of Preeclampsia Using Statistical Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly prevalent, in today's world. Machine learning techniques play a role, in the healthcare field as a whole and particularly, in the areas of obstetrics and gynecology. More specifically, methods in machine learning can be used to enhance the health and well-being of pregnant women, closely monitoring their health parameters during pregnancy. In this paper, we present a solution for predicting the risk of preeclampsia, a life-threatening disorder affecting women during pregnancy. For this purpose, we collected data from three gynaecologist in Pakistan providing health services in low resource settings in which data has samples of 233 pregnant women using 13 features which are analysed during routine checkups. We adopted model comparison approach where we trained and tested our data on multiple classification models. Performance of each model was tested in terms of accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score. On the basis of these metrics, logistic regression and XGBoost were found to be the best performing models with the accuracy of 85%.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Inter-Domain Routing Based on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning on Heterogeneous Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: To address the increasing complexity of heterogeneous networks, especially for applications such as telemedicine and autonomous driving, this study introduces a novel operational framework for efficient multi-modal, multi-objective inter-domain routing. While existing research has largely focused on multi-objective inter-domain routing, significant challenges remain in meeting multi-modal demands. Moreover, reinforcement learning-based routing algorithms often encounter issues with slow convergence and limited efficiency. This framework combines a multi-modal dung beetle optimizer with a multi-agent, multi-modal deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithm. The dung beetle optimizer mitigates the convergence and efficiency limitations of current routing algorithms by creating a high-dimensional action space, which the DRL algorithm leverages to enhance routing performance. Experimental results show a 30% increase in throughput, 25% reduction in latency, and 20% decrease in packet loss, highlighting the framework's potential for advancing multimodal routing.
